translation: Medical Mirror

text:
東醫寶鑑雜病篇卷之七

御醫忠勤貞亮居
疫癘
圣功臣崇祿大夫陽平君臣許浚奉 教撰

疫癘之源

盡形之弱而內日因於燥穴夏傷於暑秋為痎瘧。
寒熱之內問名不得通暑熱乃生世寒發膿為瘧風癘。又
則層熟之淺近而日得於理暑開乃得乱濁氣。夏汗不
也傷之後知夫而內通暑熱外寒傷膜熟為於瘧風汗出
於氣是而行傷得近而死者遠傷而瘧不能深秋則必瘧
因鬱內而衛之至夏而暑傷之瘧寒也閉鬱而後之發瘧泔
發風感冒而目者暑濕瘧也閉而發之非暑合邪瘧
早因寒并而離得之者風寒也在所附於外多
發背則發則發風離日病止在陽則發熱在在頭氣术
在血則晝或發腰難上日深則止故有時熱在在太項則
或發脊離下則遠近之不同在太陽則
translation:
Dongui Bogam (Treasured Mirror of Eastern Medicine), Miscellaneous Diseases Section, Volume 7

Royal Physician, Loyal, Diligent, and Upright Courtier
Epidemic Pestilence (Yeokryeo)
Meritorious Subject, Senior First Rank, Lord of Yangpyeong, Subject Heo Jun, composed by Royal Command

The Origins of Epidemic Pestilence

When the body is weakened internally, and one is harmed by dryness — when summer heat injures the body, autumn brings intermittent fever and malaria. When cold and heat contend internally and there is no free passage, summerheat generates pestilence and wind-malaria. When the layers of heat are shallow and the summerheat grows excessive each day, chaotic turbid qi is generated. When summer sweat cannot issue forth, when internal heat is blocked by external cold, the membranes are damaged and malaria arises. When qi is stagnant and defensive qi cannot circulate, reaching summer with summerheat — the cold closes in, causing the malaria to flare up. Due to wind-cold striking together, one contracts wind-cold malaria. When it is located on the exterior, early onset appears on the back or in the blood. When it occurs in the daytime, fever arises; when it goes deep, the fever stops at a fixed time. When located in the greater yang (taiyang) channel, it presents at the head and nape of the neck, in the upper and lower regions, varying in proximity — this is the pattern of taiyang.

text:
瘧疾形證

一也瘧。大法風暑當發汗夏月多在瘧寒之歌

又曰瘧久有變而不為瘧狀故也傷寒則傷寒久始發為勞之旁瘧然則寒疾久疾乃作嗯破渴鼓

逕在內日瘧之狀欲飲也移飲公於腰脊並於。欲陽公並陽領巨陽虛骨則腰背痛頭三而痛上去先起外毛皆伸欠乃作寒慄鼓頷腰脊俱痛寒去則外實內虛實上則陽虛陽虛則寒爭外內虛陽熱氣盛勝則寒先陽爭則盛之欲飲時令盛勝陰則陰氣當是故氣逆遵極則陽復而出陽

虛而則渴之虛阻並盛外也熟也。夫陰之外也。夫陽衰則腰痛背強三而俱阻則陰陽熟於頭中三俱同並於陽則熟並於陰則寒陰陽俱虛則寒慄鼓頷也先熱也并寒熱熱相等

也則衛行到病所不通乃作於內也寒戰鼓頷夜行相寒熱多相兼炎炎半陰寒熱則先熱勝陰先陽復表

腰背俱痛此邪氣入於作寒也寒戰鼓頷巳內外皆熱
translation:
Forms and Symptoms of Malaria (Nüeji)

First: Malaria. The general principle is that wind-heat malaria should be treated by inducing sweating. In summer months, malaria commonly manifests with alternating chills and fever — this is the hallmark pattern.

It is also said: When malaria persists for a long time, it may transform and no longer present as ordinary malaria in appearance. This is because prolonged cold damage (shanghan) that has lasted long begins to manifest as a consumptive lateral malaria (lao nüe). Thus, when a cold illness or febrile illness persists and then causes thirst and drum-like distension...

The internal daily malaria presents as: the patient wants to drink; the pathogenic qi shifts and converges at the lumbar spine, and also converges with the yang channels. When the yang of the greater yang (taiyang) is deficient and the bones are affected, there is pain in the lumbar back and head. The cold first rises from the outer skin and hair; the patient stretches and yawns, then develops chills and shivering, the jaw chatters, and the lumbar spine aches all over. When the cold departs, the exterior becomes replete and the interior becomes deficient. When the replete qi rises, the yang becomes deficient; yang deficiency leads to cold. When the exterior and interior struggle, the yang becomes exuberant, causing the patient to want to drink. At the height of exuberance, yin is overcome, and because the qi counterflows and reaches its extreme, yang recovers and comes outward.

When deficiency leads to thirst, and yin and yang both become exuberant externally, heat results. When yin is externally depleted, and the yang declines, there is lumbar pain and back stiffness. When yin and yang both converge in the head, if they converge toward yang then there is heat; if they converge toward yin then there is cold. When both yin and yang are deficient together, there is cold shivering and chattering of the jaw. If heat comes first, then cold and heat are mixed. When heat and cold are equal...

When the defensive qi (wei qi) flows and reaches the diseased location but cannot pass through, the condition manifests internally as cold shivering and chattering of the jaw. Night-time cycling of cold and heat: when cold is predominant, the defensive qi is obstructed; when heat is more prevalent, yang increases. When there is deficiency, yin prevails first, then the yang recovers to the surface.

When the pathogenic qi is more, cold is more predominant; when defensive qi is more, there is more heat. When half the qi is deficient, yin prevails first, then heat follows. When the pathogenic qi enters inward, there is cold. Cold shivering and jaw-chattering cease, and then both interior and exterior become hot.

text:
脈法

頭痛如破暑癘單熱癘煩癘多欲吐自汗此邪先寒後熱發風於

外也先寒熱飲數弦應先先寒熱後寒可以弦數多鬆弦緊者數多可遷止發汗浮弦大小脈可有宜下之弦之

數弦應為者自弦之數多鬆弦者可遷發寒弦多數弦數弦之

則數為者應風時發也則以緩飲食綠色癘。腸脈止之弦弦遲多寒弦弦之大癘多帶弦弦數數

多寒則陽風而愛遷癘脈多但弦而無帶力以數數

時寒帶可不也弦然弦短亦有。癘脈久而多脈弦但熱則弦而無帶力以數數

察手寒多則陽風而帶遷癘也。久病脈弦中見其弦多但虛微則虛損微手力以無耳力以數數

遲為癘病靈自。癘脈弦也有病脈弦中見極虛多微捕手無耳力以細

者癘理先開發因就遇夏者由夏之於大暑藏其汗大膝出

皮膚之中秋傷於風以時先傷於寒癘後傷於寒。而後後寒亦以時作名先

寒熱。而先寒後先者陰氣也後以氣也後以氣也後以歟風

也病成矣夫寒者陰氣也夏陰氣藏於水大理

傷也者皮膚之陽氣也中秋傷於風發因後遇夏病成矣於大

寒熱先後
translation:
Pulse Methods (Pulse Diagnosis)

Headache as if the head will burst, summerheat pestilence, single-heat pestilence, vexing pestilence, frequent desire to vomit, spontaneous sweating — this is pathogenic qi: first cold, then heat, manifesting as wind from the exterior.

First chills and fever with drinking: a rapid wiry pulse responds first to cold and heat. After cold one can use wiry-rapid [treatment]; many loose-wiry tight pulses indicate rapid [progression] which can be redirected to stop, promoting sweating. Floating-wiry, large and small pulses indicate it is appropriate to purge downward; wiry pulses indicate [certain conditions].

A rapid wiry pulse responding for the patient: the patient's own wiry [pulse], numerous loose-wiry [pulses] can be redirected, generating cold; wiry with many rapid-wiry beats.

Then numerous indicate: responding to wind at the time of onset, then using slow [approach] for eating and drinking, with greenish pestilence. In the intestinal pulse, stopping [pathogenic movement]: wiry pulses with delayed, numerous cold-wiry beats; large pestilence with many belt-like wiry, rapid-wiry pulses.

Many cold signs then yang-wind, with love of slow movement in pestilence; the pulse has many but only wiry without belt-force, [assessed] by counting beats.

When cold comes with belt-like [quality] it is not allowable: wiry, then short-wiry, also having pestilence pulse for a long time with many wiry [beats]; but heat then shows wiry without belt-force, by counting.

Examining the hands: cold with much yang-wind and belt-like slow pestilence. A long-standing illness with wiry pulse, in the middle seeing extremely deficient and faint — this is deficiency-damage, faint in the hands with no strength, by counting.

Slow indicates pestilence disease; the spirit is self-[contained]. The pestilence pulse is wiry; there is illness with a wiry pulse in the middle showing extreme deficiency, faint, catching the hand with no strength, faint.

The patient's illness: skin qi in autumn, injured by wind; at times first injured by cold pestilence, then injured by cold. Afterward cold again at certain times acts [upon the body] — this is named cold-heat [alternation].

First cold then heat. Those who show cold first then [heat] have yin qi. After [comes] qi, and after that qi again, and after that yin-wind.

The illness forms thus: cold is yin qi; in summer yin qi is stored in the water's great principle.

The injured: the yang qi of the skin; in mid-autumn injured by wind, manifesting because afterward encountering summer — the illness forms, coming from great [heat].

Cold-Heat: Earlier and Later

text:
寒熱往來

曰也發則少氣煩寃其但手足熱而不寒嘔者名曰陰氣先絕陽氣獨

則瘧有洒洒從術惡寒而復發熱者何也曰陰脈不足陽往從之陽脈不足陰往乘之何謂陽不足曰陽脈微則惡寒陰脈弱則惡熱陰中不足陽往乘之則發熱也陽中不足陰往乘之則發寒也

足假令足陽微足陰越陰中則發熱也假令足陽脈不足足陰往乘之則發寒也

不足則象熱陰往而發熱陽上從陽之乃勝而熱也o故陽從熱入陰則惡寒陰中則熱微陽內微陰則惡寒發熱陰

不不足則陰正邪相爭而陰勝乃無勝而寒也

不先入則則陰邪出之而表也與陰相爭則邪多熱乃則乍寒而熱也

邪不足入表而與裹相爭也與陽爭則陰邪爭在多熱而陽勝乃爲寒也

則邪多先半寒不半陽發少熱陽也則寒熱相等邪在半表

明者大陽金燥也少陽之邪在其中前後膝脛水陽

身後為行明陽則發o

寒門順o熟則多先表陰半不正邪不入也而則出之而裹也與陽相爭也有多則則乍則寒來多之氣也行之氣不也逍行也明陽o發作之間邪也則足若
translation:
Alternating Chills and Fever

It is said: When there is a deficiency, there will be shortness of breath, vexation, and distress. If the hands and feet are hot but there are no chills, and the person vomits, this is called "Yin qi cut off first, Yang qi isolated."

When there is malarial disease with shivering chills followed by renewed fever, what is the cause? It is said: When the Yin vessels are insufficient, Yang follows and enters them; when the Yang vessels are insufficient, Yin follows and overtakes them. What is meant by Yang insufficiency? It is said: When the Yang pulse is faint, there will be chills; when the Yin pulse is weak, there will be heat. When the interior Yin is insufficient and Yang comes to overtake it, fever develops. When the interior Yang is insufficient and Yin comes to overtake it, chills develop.

For example, when the foot Yang is faint and Yin surpasses it internally, fever develops. When the foot Yang pulse is insufficient and foot Yin overtakes it, chills develop.

When there is insufficiency, heat is manifested; when Yin moves forward, fever arises; Yang rises following Yang, then overcomes and produces heat. Therefore when Yang follows heat inward into Yin, chills result; when in the interior of Yin, heat is mild; when Yang is internally diminished and Yin prevails, alternating chills and fever occur.

When there is insufficiency, the upright qi and pathogenic qi contend, and when Yin prevails, there is no overcoming and chills result.

When the pathogen first enters, Yin expels it outward to the exterior; contending with Yin, the pathogen and heat fluctuate, producing alternating chills and heat.

When the pathogen is insufficient to enter the exterior and contends with the interior, competing with Yang, the Yin pathogen contends and heat increases; when Yang prevails, there is cold.

When the pathogen is half in the exterior and half in the interior, with equal chills and heat, the pathogen resides at the halfway point between exterior and interior — this is the Shaoyang pattern. The pathogen resides between the front and back, in the region of the knees and lower legs.

text:
瘧發日數多少

則惡寒近前陽失守眞邪則發熱故為往來寒熱互迭

○則甚者休作無時○休者內外陽失明燥則不分陰陽故往來寒熱也

定時矣休作有時以皮膚之內陽氣含胃因於秋暑過盛藏之以溶水氣內薄陰氣夜行於外則內外相離則病作與陽並則發熱與陰並則發寒邪正分爭兩不相勝則相繼以行於外外相離則是行

其皮膚陰陽之際得與之衝外出居於陽得陽氣盛而者薄日一行其間與邪相集五并則熱病作離於陽相陰邪則內外相薄夜行於

病以休其弄间陰則與邪并則寒弄已由至寒邪與氣內薄則衛氣日行数或至数不得連復病間也原也離則因束而順則連縣病間也

離其道也遠時不能有能與衛氣日二衛氣或供至行截合於橫則連復病幕故故皆出䆗或問

乃有其時何也不日其能相得故或数日或不甚得故邪氣與日發隆發乃至故休或溺日刀作氣発也宦次或问三者六或問

不日府而更有此时住相失也或其年不甚连○白三

陰而陽更勝也陽發者一受病二一年連發住一發陰經受病也一月發隆

也發又一三日受者氣病也最重㗢氣病陽很為府
translation:
On the Number of Days Between Malarial Attacks

When there is aversion to cold, it is because the yang qi of the front has lost its guardian, the true qi, and the pathogenic qi then generates heat; this is how alternating chills and fever arise.

In severe cases, the episodes occur without fixed timing. When there is a resting period, it means the internal and external yang has lost its clarity, causing undifferentiated yin and yang, hence the alternating chills and fever.

When attacks occur at fixed times: the yang qi contained within the skin and stomach, having been caused by the excess of autumn heat stored within, dissolves through the water qi internally pressing against the yin qi. At night it moves outward; when internal and external separate, the disease manifests. When combined with yang, fever results; when combined with yin, chills result. As the pathogenic and righteous qi contend, neither prevailing, they alternate in moving outward. When they separate, this outward movement continues.

At the boundary of yin and yang within the skin, the qi surges outward into the yang. When yang qi flourishes and the pathogenic qi is pressed daily, the pathogenic and wei qi meet and combine — when the five qi merge, the febrile attack manifests. When separated from yang and combined with yin, the pathogenic qi presses internally causing both internal and external compression, moving nocturnally outward.

The disease rests when... the pathogenic qi combines with yin causing chills; once the chill passes, it rises from cold. The pathogenic qi presses internally against the wei qi, which moves daily; after several days it may fail to connect and the disease interval appears.

When the pathway is distant, the timing may be irregular and unable to meet with the daily movement of wei qi; after two cycles, the wei qi at certain points converges where it crosses, causing continuous recurrence and the disease interval to close, with all forms appearing in various cycles of three, six, or other intervals.

When yang prevails over yin, and yin in turn prevails over yang, the yang-type attack: first the disease is received, then in one year continuous attacks occur. The yin channel receiving the disease: monthly attacks of the yin type occur.

Among these, qi diseases are the most severe. Yang qi pathology resides in the府.

text:
瘧發有書夜早晏之異

邪淺與榮衛並行一日一發。間日蓄積乃發或三四連

寒原不能與正氣並行故作日晏其作日早者何也風府下容日明乃發於日也府下每其容亦府而循膂內行日益高以節二十伏以此風府下一病入邪氣入府會合邪大客亦先夜客大則邪氣入於風府日下節三十五日此日脈益其內行骨高出於六鈇金入之邪淺中脊留衛與晝行腠背故作也腎故脈益其日次節下晝發夜行攀深也早上至則行膩精理開益也晝則其陳也邪理也開也此一晏也邪氣客則先夜客大岐伯日其作日

必日為一應發母久則使日然其作日晏

下則其衛氣也一鬢前所膜下也

或早發時為岫也九骨出十發至夜淺中脊府注日次高以節故脈益其內行也或子發時至午發定者陰陽在外也陽瘧載陽卯不而分退也用末頋升散攀中為也

在在内越越或子而分至千也者邪在至子至血分也或至外也陽從千至酉發瘧者邪散

實在發內者知邪真在至于子發也或或時分定者陰陽然後謂如發陰瘧陽不眼法與晝行背故作也腎故
translation:
On the Differences Between Malaria Attacks Occurring in the Day or Night, Early or Late

When the pathogenic influence is superficial, it travels together with the nutritive and defensive qi, causing a fever once every day. When it accumulates over an interval of days it then erupts, sometimes every third or fourth day in succession.

When the cold originates from a place where it cannot travel together with the upright qi, it causes the attack to occur later in the day. As for why some attacks occur early in the day — the Wind Mansion point receives the wind daily, becoming apparent, and the attack arises during the daytime. Beneath the mansion, the wind lodges there every day, and also lodges in the mansion, circulating along the spine inward, each day rising higher through the joints. After twenty-five days it descends below the Wind Mansion joint; after thirty-five days this daily pulse increases, moving inward through the bones, emerging at the sixth vertebra, entering with the pathogenic influence at a shallow level of the spine. Staying in the defensive qi as it circulates during the day through the interstices of the back, it therefore triggers an attack. The kidney pulse increases, circulating through the joints below, causing daytime attacks. The pathogenic influence goes deep into the nighttime, causing the attack to be late.

When qi rises upward and the defensive qi moves, the fine textures open and the daytime passages become clear — this causes a late attack. The pathogenic influence lodges and first settles at night.

Whether the attack begins at the hour of Zi and extends to Wu, or is fixed — this is because yin and yang are externally present. Yang malaria carries yang outward; at Mao it no longer separates, and it withdraws. Using the method of dispersing from the center accomplishes this.

In the interior, the pathogenic influence from Zi to Xu at the blood level, or extending outward — for those whose malaria attacks from the hour of Zi through You, the pathogenic influence disperses.

Those with attacks in the interior know that the pathogenic influence reaches Zi and the attack begins, or at a fixed interval — this is because yin and yang afterward cause the yin malaria and yang qi to not reach the eyes and the method applies to daytime circulation along the back, thus triggering the attack in the kidneys.

六經瘧

夏傷於暑秋必病瘧者有三陽者初不知何經受病其邪在三陽經者謂之三陽瘧治之以三陽受邪在三陰者謂之三陰瘧治之以三陰各有所治之法凡熱多寒少瘧者近病皆謂之陽暑多謂之陽瘧治法宜清暑和解此近病者也暴謄也後在陰經在冬至前者至夏至前謂之日瘧故冬陰在後陰經者汗之謂之瘧經者謂之在寒少陽治大越多汗經受

translation:
Six-Channel Malaria

When summer heat injures the body, malaria will necessarily occur in autumn. There are three yang types — at first it is unknown which channel has received the pathogen. When the pathogen is lodged in the three yang channels, it is called three-yang malaria and is treated according to the three-yang method. When the pathogen is lodged in the three yin channels, it is called three-yin malaria and is treated according to the three-yin method. Each has its own treatment principle. In general, malaria with more heat and less chills is a recent condition, all called yang malaria; when heat from summer is predominant, it is called yang malaria. The treatment principle should be to clear summer heat and harmonize. This applies to recent conditions.

For wind malaria, wind-cold malaria, warm malaria, and pestilential malaria — each has its corresponding formula. When heat is great and cold is slight, the treatment should harmonize and warm the yang. When the condition involves the Yangming channel, use Yangming-warming decoctions. Formulas involving Bupleurum (Chaihu), Ginseng (Renshen), Cinnamon twig (Guizhi), Atractylodes (Baizhu), and similar herbs are selected depending on which channel is affected — whether Taiyang, Yangming, or Shaoyang — and whether sweating, vomiting, or purging is indicated.

For combined three-yang channel diseases, harmonize using the appropriate combined formula. For cases presenting with spontaneous sweating, headache, neck stiffness, and lumbar-spinal rigidity, use Guizhi decoction base.

Guizhi Qianghuo Qufeng Decoction: Qianghuo (notopterygium), Fangfeng (saposhnikovia), Gancao (licorice) — one qian and a half each. Cut into one packet, decoct in water.

translation:
[Preparation and Administration]

Mahuang Qianghuo Decoction: Treats Taiyang deficiency malaria with absence of sweating. This is the same as the previous formula but removes Guizhi (cinnamon twig).

Chaihu Guizhi Decoction: Treats Shaoyang malaria with alternating chills and fever. The preparation and administration method is the same as above. Remove Chaihu 2 qian, Gui 2 qian, Gancao 5 fen.

Chaihu Plus Gui Decoction: Treats Shaoyang malaria with alternating chills and fever — extremely effective. [Contains] Banxia 1 qian, Gancao 4 fen, Huang[qi]... 3 fen. Take one dose in water, decoct, and drink warm with tea. For Yangmalaria, see relevant section. Two doses: Banxia 1 qian, Gancao 4 fen, Huang[qi]... Guizhi...

Baihu Guizhi Decoction: Combines Shigao 4 [liang], prepared and applied. Decoct in water, drink warm. For seasonal malaria where the pulse feels normal, the body has no chills but only fever, resolving in the morning and recurring at dusk; resolving in the morning — this medicine governs agitation.

Mahuang Baizhu Decoction: [Mix ingredients in pot with] Gancao 3-7 fen each, decoct in water and take. [Contains] Fuling, Baizhu, Jiegeng, Xixin... Right side: 4 doses treat Banxia wind sores. Zihuang, Guipi, Chipi, Qingpi, Chenpi, Chuanguizhi, Bai[zhu], Yi[ren], Gancao, add or reduce 1 qian, Guizhi, Jiegeng...

translation:
Chaihu Siwu Tang (Bupleurum Four Substances Decoction): Treats malarial fever of the three yin meridians, or those with fever occurring at night. Ingredients: bupleurum, dried rehmannia, red peony root, 3 qian each; ginseng, pinellia, scutellaria, licorice, ligusticum, angelica root, 2 qian each. Prepare one dose, divide into eight portions, decoct and take.

Guizhi Shaoyao Tang (Cinnamon Twig and Peony Decoction): Treats severe malarial alternating chills and fever, with pronounced heat and flushing. This is a combined disease of taiyang and yangming, characterized by sweating without recovery. When there is severe alternating chills and heat with flushing, if anemarrhena is not used, one fears that prolonged jaundice will spread throughout.

Guizhi Shigao Tang (Cinnamon Twig and Gypsum Decoction): [Dosage:] 2 qian of water, decoct and take as directed. [Used for] taiyang-yangming combined disease with intermittent episodes. Anemarrhena, 3 qian. Pinellia. Much cinnamon twig, little gypsum, 1 qian each on the right.

Guizhi Huangqin Tang (Cinnamon Twig and Scutellaria Decoction): Divided preparation, one gate dose. Cinnamon twig and peony combination decoction, for post-illness reversion where chills and fever worsen. Anemarrhena, bupleurum, taiyang formula. Ginseng, pinellia, licorice, 2 qian each. Junzi Tang (Gentlemen Decoction), decoct and take, to replenish and supplement the middle.

For malarial fever occurring during the day versus at night, treatment should be differentiated. For qi deficiency with daytime fever, use Yiqi (Qi-Boosting) formula; add pinellia and scutellaria. For blood deficiency and obstruction, supplement the middle.

translation:
Night Grain [indications]

Mahuang Qin Decoction (Ephedra and Scutellaria Decoction)
Decoction Grain Section — Chaihu Siwu Decoction (Bupleurum Four Substances Decoction) — Formula
Mahuang (Ephedra), Huangqin (Scutellaria) 1 qian each; Chaihu (Bupleurum); Taoren Chengqi (Peach Kernel Qi-Coordinating) 2 qian; Gancao (Licorice) 1 qian

Apply powder decoction; take at the time of serving. Guixin 1 qian, Taoren (Peach Kernel) 10–15 pieces. Right: cut and prepare with Gancao 1 qian.

[Instruction]: Decoct in water and take before the [fever] episode. Peach kernel has a bitter and sweet-acrid flavor entering the Liver Channel. As it works through blood pathways of the Sea [of Blood], it soothes Liver Qi. This is the meaning of "when there is urgency, eat sweet flavors to relieve it." Therefore this is indicated for Yin Channel blood disorders.

This formula uses Huanggan (Liver-clearing) decoction meaning: for pathogenic Qi that has gone deep, causing fever with blood entering the middle, wind-cold night attacks.

[With] kernel — treats the night Yin pattern, drawing [pathogenic qi] out from the Yang level and dispersing it. After taking, add Renshen (Ginseng).

Chaihu Gui Decoction (Bupleurum and Angelica Decoction)
Honghua (Safflower), Danggui (Angelica), Chishao (Red Peony) — cuts off night fever, stops Yin patterns; Houpo (Magnolia bark), Chaihu (Bupleurum), dry Yang-level Chuanxiong (Ligusticum). Each: after taking, 1 qian Renshen (Ginseng).
Gancao (Licorice), each 3 qian portions. Right: cut and make one packet. Baizhu 8 liang, Chuanxiong 1 qian, Chenpi 2 he, Meizi 7 fen, Jiegeng 1 fen.

Take by decocting in water.

Treatment of Various Types of Malaria (Nüe)
Wind Malaria: contracted from wind. Types of malaria include: Wind Malaria, Cold Malaria, Phlegm Malaria, Chronic Malaria, Fatigue Malaria, Food Malaria.
Contracted from cold: Heat Malaria, Fatigue-Phlegm Malaria, Phlegm [Malaria].

Cold Malaria: use Fruit Appendage Decoction; frequent fruit drinks; Chaihu Guijiang Decoction nourishes Stomach Qi — named Rumian Malaria, see Cross-Resolution [section].
Wind Malaria: contracted from wind, producing heat followed by chills — use Mahuang Baizhu Zhengqi Decoction [see] section.

translation:
热疟 (Heat Malaria): Caused by summer-heat, with a wiry pulse, much fever and heat, contracted in such manner. Also called Hu-malaria or Summer Malaria. It is appropriate to use Renshen Baihu Decoction (Ginseng and White Tiger Decoction).

湿疟 (Damp Malaria): Caused by exposure to dampness; there is difficulty with urination. The five-powder formula is indicated. Sweating occurs, and upon hearing of malaria one seeks a bath. There is alternating chills and fever, difficulty with urination; one uses Chaihu (Bupleurum) Decoction with attachments; if prolonged, modify accordingly.

痰疟 (Phlegm Malaria): Does not stop. Use Erchen Decoction, Chai-Zan Decoction combined; add to this the wormwood head formula; or use Chuantao formula; when eating and swallowing becomes difficult, the phlegm malaria beans cause vomiting; attach the decoction and if prolonged, advance by one strange method.

食疟 (Food Malaria): Also known as Stomach-Cold Malaria or Reversion Malaria. Caused by heat and cold imbalance; one should restore equilibrium. When food supply is disrupted, the patient starves yet cannot eat; there is no injury, but cold accumulates; once balance is restored, vomiting clears, recovery and return follow.

劳疟 (Taxation Malaria): Treatment is from both exterior and interior. When malaria is severe, with cold in the origin and center, it is difficult to resolve; heat and fever persist, then briefly abate, only for cold to return — this is most difficult to regulate. Use the decoction with added Chenpi (tangerine peel), or with Liuyang, Suosha (cardamom), small beans, and scallion decoction; again add Atractylodes; if pus and swelling forms, use the child-day spirit formula to promote vomiting and recovery.

translation:
Head [fever] not subsiding: it is appropriate to use Bow-Return Warming Armor Powder, Changshan Drink, Jade Side Pill, Liuhe Decoction, Black [Pill].

Cinnabar Pill, Nourish-Stomach Pill, Ginger, Ten Generals Decoction: one episode of chills, one episode of fever.
Blood Pill: when deficient, one feels aversion to cold; when vacuous, fever and chills alternate; when flow is disrupted, chills arise.

Shivering as if in boiling [heat], all manifesting in the spleen, or vomiting, vacuity, delayed [recovery], inability to eat, diarrhea, abdominal pain, cold extremities — Supplement the Center Qi Decoction.
Recognizing pathogenic qi invasion: the pathogen is fierce, causing rapid chills and fever; the spleen is weak, unable to eat, or there is diarrhea, abdominal pain — Supplement Center Qi Decoction.
Ghost Malaria (Guinüe): caused by invasion of pathogenic qi, manifesting as fierce chills and fever occurring daily, with fear and fright; it is appropriate [to treat accordingly].
Epidemic Malaria (Yinüe): formulas — long-standing [cases] first use染 [染 = contracted through] seasonal epidemic qi that transforms into chills and fever; one must use Yunqi [Circulating Qi methods].
[One] Center.
Medicines: it is appropriate not to use [inappropriate ones]; use Jinzhengqi Powder, Qu-Malaria Drink, Ruyi Pill, Five-Malaria Pill, Treat-Plague Formula, [Nine doses].
Miasma Malaria (Zhangnüe):
[It is caused by] mountain mist and miasmatic steaming toxic qi that causes people to become confused and delirious, or to go mad, or to suddenly feel chills.
[When] active [fever] flares from mountain miasma and steaming toxin qi, causing confusion, madness, or sudden chills —
Guanyin Decoction, Jie [Resolving] Drink, Dilong [Earthworm] Drink.
For the many diseases of this type, it is appropriate to use Double-Resolution Drink or Dilong Drink.
Southern miasma toxin.

text:
痰瘧

者日老一瘧也以其三日一發瘧於綿不去仰也腳日○三作瘧者邪入於陰經也瘧當以汗解汗得於暑經已也作瘧者邪得於陰經也當以汗解必先兆上補邪解收汗兌與典入力到得興汗作者

於少陰成丑末日作者太申已經一也瘧解術夫感冒風暑之補加刺體柔邪也非難得散保古方多風暑之補邪剖在到恐

參汗汗解於限陰成丑末日作者太申已經一也瘧解術夫感冒風寒等藥補為養君佳養兆下體柔邪也故非難得散保古方多用之嶺邪剖在到恐

并陰分宜明用○血若藥引發陽無病也時為必難得愈而大失漸期若感之邪亦必恐

自後難治故傳病者用春血發病也易為必時難愈而大失漸若感之邪亦必

乃則母有也瘧雖老內虛血結非常也九成山瘧橫柵疾於不能腹非作差有調他也老以是早發亦有是半

汗佳必之兆故為此病前至者用春夏為病發亦易時秋冬為難愈須失漸期若感之邪亦必

瘧熟用者曾不損胃雖老元瘧九以補是也化血瘧者宜輔敬甲飲之九目有量水制瘧

痺瘧用者曾不損胃雖老元瘧九以補是也七化血瘧者宜輔黨甲飲之九目有量水制瘧

參歸黨甲飲秘方○清甲瘧七化疾湯黨甲飲之補老瘧宜脾化血疾湯驚甲飲之甲九量有水制瘧
translation:
Phlegm Malaria

The text discusses malaria (瘧/학질) conditions and their treatment:

On the third-day recurring malaria (tertian malaria): This is a type of malaria that recurs every three days without ceasing. It is caused by pathogenic evil entering the yin channels. Malaria should be resolved through sweating. Sweating is obtained through the summer-heat channel. When malaria manifests, the evil has entered the yin channels, and resolution must come through sweating; one must first recognize the signs, tonify to expel the evil, and promote sweating.

Regarding malaria associated with the Shaoyin channel, manifesting at the Chou and Wei hours, or at the Shen and Si hours — this is a malaria of the channels. The technique for resolving it involves: when one has contracted wind-cold or summerheat, medicines should tonify and nourish the condition. If the body is weakened by pathogenic evil, it is difficult to disperse and preserve; ancient formulas frequently used such approaches, but with severe pathogenic evil present, one must be cautious.

On treatment: When yin is divided, it is appropriate to use clear prescriptions. If blood-moving medicines are used to induce a yang outbreak without addressing the disease, it becomes difficult to achieve a cure and the condition will gradually worsen. If evil pathogen is contracted, it is certainly to be feared.

On phlegm-malaria with heat: Formulas used should not damage the stomach. Though the patient is old and constitutionally deficient, the Nine-Tonification Malaria Pill is appropriate. For blood-type malaria, use Supplementing Biejia (turtle shell) Decoction, Danggui Biejia Drink, calculated by the appropriate water dosage.

Primary formulas: Qingpijia Decoction, Danggui Biejia Drink — for chronic malaria with spleen deficiency and blood stasis, use Huaxue Malaria Decoction and Biejia Drink, adjusting the Biejia dosage with water preparation.

translation:
Scatter Pathogen Decoction (散邪湯)
One packet per dose.
Take warm in the morning after overnight preparation.
Decoct with three [cups of water]: Qianghuo (notopterygium root) — for initial onset of wind-cold;
Baizhi (angelica root), Suhuang (perilla yellow), Baishao (white peony), Fangfeng (saposhnikovia root) — 1 qian each; Gancao (licorice) — 5 fen. Cut and prepare as directed.

Rectify Qi Decoction (正氣湯)
Decoct as above.
Qingpi (green tangerine peel), Qianhu (hogfennel root), Chuanxiong, Baizhi (angelica root), Banxia (pinellia), Maidong (ophiopogon), Guizhi (cinnamon twig), Gancao (licorice) — 1 qian each; Chifuling (red poria) — 1 qian and a half.

Jiafu Drink (交附飲)
Cut into pieces and divide into two doses.
Decoct in water and take. [Used for] double-cold patterns and various accumulation disorders.
Treats obesity with phlegm accumulation: Qingpi (green tangerine peel), Hangrass, seven jujubes, Fuzi (aconite, roasted) — equal parts, two doses; decoct with Zisuye (perilla leaf).

Caoguo Drink (草果飲)
Treats cold pathogen lodged internally: Guoliangjiang (lesser galangal), Caogu (tsaoko fruit), Qingpi (green tangerine peel), water, Chuanxiong, decocted with Zisuye (perilla leaf) — 3 qian each.

Chaihu Ginger Decoction (柴胡薑湯)
Cut and prepare; ginger — 8 fen per dose; Muli (oyster shell) — for alternating chills and fever; Banxia (pinellia), Tianhuafen (trichosanthes root), Yanhuo (tested), Huangbai, Chaihu (bupleurum) — 3 qian each.

Chaihu Zhimu Decoction (柴胡知母湯)
Cut and prepare; one piece of ginger; Gancao — 8 fen per dose; Guizhi (cinnamon twig), Biejia (turtle shell, roasted) — 1 qian each; [for] heat and accumulation patterns; Chaihu (bupleurum), Zhimu (anemarrhena) — 1 qian and a half each; Gancao, Ganjiang (dry ginger), Huangcha (yellow tea), Gancao (licorice), Chenpi (tangerine peel), Banxia (pinellia), Chuanxiong — 1 qian and a half each.

translation:
Herb Roasted [seven fen], right: cut and prepare one dose, apply ginger three pieces, plum two pieces, decoct in water once.

争功San (Contending Merit Powder)
Treats [conditions]: add and apply, passing through eight pathways — peach bark, rehmannia, cortex lycii, licorice, anemarrhena, each one qian; additionally for urinary obstruction: cicada slough two, bupleurum, scrophularia, anemarrhena, Changshan — cut and prepare as one dose [with] willow.

Longhu Tang (Dragon-Tiger Decoction)
Treats [various conditions using]: citrus, indigo paste, fire-processed, half a small bowl [of liquid]; rolled up with bupleurum, lips, nose, forsythia, each as needed; six portions of the base, half [qian of] scutellaria; pulse indicators: flooding and tight.

Xiao Qing Pi Tang (Minor Clear Spleen Decoction)
For treating stomach conditions monthly: cao, pu 2 qian each, 5 fen, right side ban xia, prepared with qing pi, applied with ginger.

Yanwei Dan (Stomach-Nourishing Pill)
Treats chronic pestilential illness of two to three years that has not healed. Ingredients: Various fruits, 2 liang; Dried ginger, 1 liang and a half; Honey-processed [herb], 9 qian; Jade citrus peel, 4 qian; Atractylodes (Cangzhu); Mountain cornelian cherry, wine-steamed, 2 liang; Dried ginger, 9 pieces; Various grasses, 2 portions; Realgar, fine-ground; Water-ground realgar.

Suixie Dan (Crushing Evil Pill)
Treats pestilential illness. Ingredients: Mixed in equal portions. Half a qian treats water-pestilence. To treat ghost-pestilence: Separately grind yellow beans (large soybeans), realgar, black beans, peach kernels, 7 pieces, ground fine. Each day at sunrise, take one pill washed down with realgar water. Take from the east and south directions during winter solstice periods. Each 9 pills, the young and strong may take fewer. Grind arsenic finely; dry and store.

Xiongzhu Dan (Realgar-Cinnabar Pill)
Treats ghost-pestilence. Use black bean paste to make pills; take 49 pills each day at sunrise. Take from the east, collecting from the east-south direction twice during winter, each 9 pills. The young and strong take fewer. Dry, store, use slow fire; arsenic used with caution.

Shuangjie Yinzi (Double-Resolution Drink)
Especially effective when illness first breaks out. Treats pestilence. Warm the body; soothe with divine [remedy]; for cold-type pestilence, use one dose. Mix realgar and cinnabar as coating; dry in sun and store. Large-dose arsenic preparation.

Moxa at the empty-heart point (one cun). Use: Licorice, 2 liang; Gypsum, 2 liang; Raw aconite, half raw; Fresh ginger; each in portions; apply as poultice, insert dates and stems; fresh ginger water decoction.

Jiaojie Drink, also called Fresh Ginger Decoction Drink, also called Fresh Ginger Boiled Drink — taken frequently. Also named Fresh Ginger Boiled Drink.

Ground Dragon Drink (Di Long Yin)
Treats hives with great heat, flushed and inflamed cheeks. Use a small amount each of: borneol (dragon brain), peppermint juice, fresh ginger juice. For adults, use three portions with freshly drawn water; grind finely and take dissolved in water.

Qianghuo Atractylodes Decoction (Qiang Huo Cang Zhu Tang)
Take equal amounts with 5 slices of ginger. Chop the ingredients, add water, and decoct as firewood-fire煎. Take orally. Ingredients: coptis root (hu huang), scutellaria (qin), bitter orange (zhi shi). Treats alternating chills and fever with hives and redness. Pinellia (ban xia), treats [conditions], one and a half qian. Ginger, three portions. Sichuan [herb] number. Licorice root (gan cao).

Guanyin Pill (Guan Yin Yuan)
White [alum], immediately take with water. Treats sun-dried hives. Pinellia, raw alum, mume flesh, hemp seed, clove, croton seed flesh. Five per dose, each pill ten [units]. Take at the appropriate time.

Old Hives Pill (Lao Yin Jiu)
The method is the same as above. Treats hives caused by individual constitution. [With] sea alum horn, named for abdominal pain, there is [a dose] every [time], combined with ten liang of rhubarb (jiang jun). Take nine doses together.

Egret Shell Pill (Lu Jia Jiu)
Nine doses, named five [qian]. One qian. Grind to powder. Egret [shell], mother pill, paste with [vinegar]. Skin [preparation]. Add peach kernel, seed, red [herb], large white [herb], fermented leaven, malt, medicated vinegar, cook three liang, sea powder, and [other herbs].

The method for the nine doses is the same. Treats hives with attached [conditions], persistent hive nodules that do not resolve for a long time. Each [ingredient] taken separately. Also treats postpartum [conditions] with abdominal bloating, two portions remaining, eight flavors each one liang, with rhubarb method, nine doses taken together.

Ginseng-Stalk and Turtle-Shell Drink
Treats chronic malaria with abdominal masses that have formed into a "malaria mother" (malarialump). Turtle shell (vinegar-cooked), white poria, one plum, water, half each, decoct, take in doses. Sand (cinnabar) eight fen, ginseng, angelica root, gardenia fruit, white atractylodes, aurantium immaturus, each half qian, Ligusticum chuanxiong three fen, licorice, cyperus rhizome, each three fen; cut the above into one packet; add three slices of ginger, two jujubes, decoct in water and take.

Secret Formula Qingga Pills
Prepared as a powder and made into pills, with thick magnolia bark (houpo), five qian each, washed down with large cup of hot water, sixty to seventy pills each time; one liang each of ginseng, white atractylodes, and licorice; one and a half liang pinellia; on the third day the green tangerine peel — for attacks occurring every ten or eleven days, one dose each of ginseng, white atractylodes, and licorice.

Classically Effective Malaria Elixir
Grind into powder and mix evenly; peach kernel decoction with cinnabar pills, one dose; for alternating chills and fever with no cure; dissolve in hot water with asafoetida; grind realgar and orpiment, each two zhu; half the above ground into powder.

For malaria mother masses in the epigastrium that have long failed to heal: cinnabar, asafoetida, pangolin scales (roasted in fat).

瘧寒熱不歇有根

黑豆去皮擣或泥和九九釐稀子

大空心薑湯飲之寒熱不歇日不散血是爲關瘧者惟熱爲故之何

丹惟敗水飲日熱隨之毒水日不散血飲結而水爲必能治之

法飲血爲暑老蓄毒黃或水謹而之毒惟飲結寒療者皆能生。

兀瘧皆敗水因血取毒水去其毒於病根則吐之水寒熱在中下則亦以能瘧生。

剖寒多熱用茗常帶下也盖毒水去其上則病根則吐之水寒熱結療在自解而以能瘧

其破水其故帝也還下覆悪寒也發有如日如膕復其復發之狀或一日會速過發

寒熱似瘧

氣之時多而有陰氣少日也發陰其氣故惡寒也何發有如日復膕復其發之日陽氣勝則膕復相薄盛日表速之陽過發

translation:
Malaria with Alternating Chills and Fever That Does Not Cease — Having a Root

Black soybeans, remove the skin, pound into a paste or powder, form into pills the size of millet, take on an empty stomach with ginger decoction. When chills and fever do not cease day after day, and blood does not disperse, this is called persistent malaria (關瘧). The heat is the cause — what is the origin of this?

Drinking [medicine] — when blood becomes related to summerheat, and old accumulated toxin turns the water yellow, or when the water is carefully observed and the toxin is in the water, if drinking results in the congealing of the water-cold, the malaria can be cured.

When malaria involves defeat of water, blood takes up the toxin; the water drives out the poison. When the source of disease in the upper [body] is expelled, the patient vomits the water — when cold and heat are bound together and cure is achieved, the condition naturally resolves and the malaria can be cured.

Breaking the [toxic] water — the emperor's teaching is: when the [qi] descends again, evil cold develops, and [fever] recurs like the sun each day, the condition or each day the malaria pattern recurs. The yang qi prevails, then the [condition] flares again, competing intensely; on the day when the surface [level] rapidly flares — this is the nature of alternating-day malaria.

Malaria-like Chills and Fever

When the qi is out of balance, yin qi increases while yang qi diminishes; yin qi prevails and evil cold develops. The yang qi then surges back, and they contend with one another; when yang is strong, the surface rapidly flares — this is how malaria-like patterns manifest.

When miasmic qi is excessive and the pattern differs, treatment by ordinary methods may be ineffective; when heat predominates and the pattern shifts, one observes the patient carefully.

When only the heat pattern persists, one must not be complacent; it is necessary to treat thoroughly, paying attention to the pulse of the stomach.

For resolving and harmonizing [the pattern]: in cases of internal damage with deficiency, use Bu Zhong Yi Qi Tang (Center-Supplementing Qi-Boosting Decoction); add Ren Shen Yang Wei Tang (Ginseng Stomach-Nourishing Decoction) for effectiveness. When chills predominate, add Chaihu (Bupleurum) and ginger. When chills are severe, add Shan (Mountain) Cinnamon and Malt Sprout Decoction.

瘧疾治法

白豆蔻扶脾，自止。矢內經主於暑風，局方主於傷食，丹溪主於痰。參為要藥，木通三因於至錯，寒熱無汗，然後捷徑以柴胡湯，加烏梅消瘧。

正無汗者，熱氣散邪散，為主帶有散邪，散宜正邪，補氣湯汗，者加柴胡，要寒汗無，瘧汗不能，清解用扶。

陽草果無尊為主，村須不能溫散，胡散宜蒿熏，柴以法胡，黃茗湯，以汗者，須用清，能瘧汗，并扶。加。

熟胡升後，熟宜小芎汗多，須先用寒後，熟宜柴以，蒿無茗，汗不。須能清解，用扶。

翻熟熟宜，白虎胡湯，須先用寒，後但熟宜散，柴胡欲無，加之桂，陽薑多先，柴胡桂。分桂陰，湯加。多先柴。

寒熟○相，者挂技挂，法以陽，半多寒，後但熟宜，散柴胡欲無加之，桂陽薑減，湯多先柴。

寒則收其，疾之水則，多者作，寒之多者，先投以時，半追進以，熱熟壯乙，散分除桂，減湯多。陽薑壯，膊藥。

進慎飲食，次以藥，謹起抵，制截矣，失之。寒熟○相，甚多者，先以冷，寒但半，熟宜散柴，胡湯須，先用寒桂，陽薑多。合五蒼苓，散明。

治太陽，合白二陳，湯治食，積明小柴，胡散飲，湯少陽，意佳技，疾須明。

顧技疾，合白二，陳湯治，食積明，小攻之，惠疹矢，去少陽，意佳技，疾須明。

translation:
Methods for Treating Malaria (Ague)

White cardamom (Bai Dou Kou) supports the spleen and stops [the illness] on its own. The Inner Canon (Neijing) attributes malaria to summerheat and wind; the Bureau of Formularies (Jufang) attributes it to dietary damage; Danxi attributes it to phlegm-retention. Ginseng is the essential medicine. Mutong (akebia) addresses the three causes of alternating chills and fever. When there is no sweating, the quick treatment is Chaihu (bupleurum) decoction, with the addition of dark plum (wumei) to dispel the malarial pathogen.

When the patient has no sweating and the heat disperses the pathogen, the primary approach is to disperse the pathogen and correct it. For cases of pathogenic qi, use qi-supplementing decoction to promote sweating; add Chaihu. If there is cold without sweating, and the patient cannot sweat to clear the pathogen, use supporting herbs.

Cao Guo (tsaoko) is the primary herb for treating malarial heat; use it when warming and dispersing is needed. For cases using Artemisia and Chaihu decoctions—when the patient sweats—first clear, then resolve the pathogen, and support with additional herbs.

For cases of alternating heat and chills, regulate with Baihu (White Tiger) decoction; for cases of cold followed by heat, use Chaihu dispersing formula with cinnamon and ginger added, dividing yin and yang patterns accordingly.

For cases where cold and heat alternate severely, first administer a cold preparation, then follow with warming formulas of Chaihu and cinnamon. Adjust the decoction with ginger to balance the condition.

When cold is predominant and leads to fluid accumulation, treat the cold excess first by timing the doses appropriately. Administer warming, fortifying herbs divided with cinnamon-reducing decoctions adjusted with ginger.

Regarding diet: be cautious with food and drink; follow with medicines carefully, monitoring and cutting off [the pathogen] before it progresses. For alternating cold and heat, use cold preparations first, then warming Chaihu-cinnamon-ginger formulas. Combine with Wuling San or Cang-ling San as appropriate.

For Taiyang-pattern malaria, use a combination of Erchen (Two-Cured) Decoction for food accumulation. For Shaoyang-pattern, use Minor Chaihu Decoction modified accordingly.

For chronic or recurring malaria, use the combined Erchen Decoction formula for food accumulation; for dispersing excess, use Shaoyang-pattern modifications as appropriate.

translation:
Knowing That a Malaria Episode Is About to Resolve

When the Shaoyang pattern is recognized, one knows it can be resolved. If one knows to use Chaihu, and the chills and fever occur at a fixed time each day without shifting, this is the pathogenic qi having no place to lodge, and the evil has no room to stay.

One knows that it can resolve early. To cut off (截) malaria: if the elderly have chills and fever occurring at a fixed time each day, and the timing shifts to later, this is the evil finding no room to remain.

When malaria is about to resolve, one should know to resolve it early by intercepting the disease. If the elderly have chills and fever at a fixed time and the timing shifts or becomes later, this means the pathogenic qi has no place to lodge.

When malaria is about to resolve, after it has occurred several times and the fever comes regularly, it is appropriate to intercept it at this point. If left too long, the accumulated toxins will damage the body's vitality.

Method for Cutting Off Malaria (截瘧法)

To intercept after one or two days is ideal. Intercept when the fever recedes and the exterior symptoms respond; one may intercept using the formula. The proper time to apply the intercepting method is around the third or fourth day. The longer one waits, the harder it becomes; one must not delay day after day.

One must choose the right time to intercept. Once the fever has formed into a full malaria pattern, the intercepting decoction can be applied. The formula should be administered around the third or fourth day.

If the appetite and food intake are a concern, once the malaria pattern has taken form, the intercepting method is applied; recovery follows. Large accumulations require supportive treatment first.

For cases where the malaria has become entrenched over months and years, the intercepting approach can still lead to recovery.

For jaundice-type malaria (疸瘧), where vomiting occurs and the disease does not resolve with purgation, with hidden pathogenic factors lodged in the viscera, apply the intercepting formula.

For the intercepting malaria decoction (截瘧常山飲), the formula uses Changshan (Dichroa root) as the main herb. The dosage ratio and supporting herbs such as Renshen (ginseng) are used to cut off the malaria.

Take Croton seeds (巴豆), remove skin and oil, grind separately. Southern Official Cinnamon (官桂), grind separately. White Alum (白礬), grind separately. On the day when the moon is full, early in the morning grind all ingredients, ensuring complete stillness and purity until that day's early morning preparation, then expose to sun.

At the appropriate time when all ingredients are ready, mix and blend evenly, each three qian. For women and adults: when the moon is full, grind with stillness until the day of preparation.

At a thousand pills, first thing in the morning blend with cold water, form into pills the size of a stick, nose-apply when sudden illness occurs, with stillness.

Pill to Stop Carbuncles Like a Sage (斷癰如聖九)
Abstain from food and drink; do not make it difficult.
Grind the ingredients into powder, two qian; large water leeches, refine into pills, three pills, like simple male [black] large soybeans; come after ten days of pills.
On the left and right, stuff the ear canal; grind finely, pass over as divine; one dose early, illness will improve; add charcoal separately; continue dosing.

Prohibitions and Contraindications for Carbuncles (禁忌法癰)
During an episode, do not eat to excess or take hot food frequently; fear that it will not digest and form into hard masses. Take nine pills during flare-ups.

Conditions Difficult to Treat and Untreatable

When pustular rashes (疿) have not yet erupted, the nine-rash formula is coming and the disease is just beginning to develop — medicine cannot yet be administered. Medicine should be taken before the rash fully erupts; take the medicine at the proper time. [Instructions on dosing times.]

For flesh-type rashes, one must strictly avoid fresh pork; for bovine-type rashes, endure and avoid wind and cold. Encounter the day of eruption — take on an empty stomach in the morning; be cautious in movement and residence, and recovery will come.

Before the rash erupts, take the medicine with food or drink two hours earlier, or with alcohol avoided; on the day of eruption, take on an empty stomach in the morning.

For bovine-type rash patients who endure and avoid fresh pork, and form into nine pills — these are easy to treat. Yin-type rashes are difficult to treat. There is a milder form. Long-standing rashes that recur repeatedly, and rash diseases of long duration that cause disability —

Those who are bedridden are approaching death and cannot be treated for hot or cold conditions.

Those whose body has wasted and who have strong spasms with acute heat from the nine rashes, who cannot eat — these are difficult to treat.

Kidney deficiency with cold and heat, elderly, cinnabar pills.

translation:
Causes of Epidemic Pestilence (Wenyi)

The Inner Canon (Neijing) states: "Those who are harmed by cold in winter will necessarily develop warm disease in spring. Those who fail to store their essence in winter will necessarily fall ill with warm disease in spring." Some say this becomes disease because the world is full of pestilential warm qi that rises and forms illness. Others say it is because filth and noxious matter are not expelled. All of these are causes of this illness.

When the qi of the mountains and seas, the warm qi of rivers and the sea, and the great electrical qi of the earth all accumulate, they can cause warm disease. When celestial and terrestrial qi moves and circulates, when epidemic qi arises and surges, the warm official qi may be involved as well.

When warmth reverses and becomes non-cold, when conditions in summer turn hot yet conversely produce cold responses, when in the depths of winter there is unseasonable warmth, and in spring there is unseasonable cold — these reversals of the seasons give rise to pestilence.

When the qi of heaven and earth is not correct, or when the qi does not correspond to its proper season, yet epidemic qi arises — this is what is called "seasonal epidemic" (shixing). This is the great reversal.

Some say: when heaven and earth hold incorrect qi, and when this qi does not accord with its proper season, it manifests as a demonic influence. These are the causes of pestilence.

Signs and Symptoms of Epidemic Pestilence

When in winter the body contracts and cannot stretch, and then in spring warmth arises as epidemic warm disease, the symptoms seen during the day include: rash or eruptions, lumbar pain, severe chills and acute fever.

translation:
Pulse Method (Pulse Diagnosis)

[This page is from a section on pulse diagnosis related to febrile and epidemic diseases. The text discusses the following:]

On recovering from spontaneous fever; prohibitions; spring warmth counterflow; summer outbreaks with throat symptoms; physical symptoms including neck stiffness, skin and flesh involvement.

In autumn, qi merges; coughing and throat symptoms appear; yin affects both sides of the body; heat spreads to the skin and muscles, causing rigidity and painful obstruction.

When heat arises at the height of a disease, the lips, eyes, and vision become clouded; the throat is affected; drinking and eating become impaired; heat toxin spreads.

The superficial and slippery pulse is associated with conditions where the name "sinking warm disease" applies. When yin and yang pulses are both excessive, there is no fever — this is a sign of epidemic disease.

As the illness transforms and the pulse becomes straight and taut, by the eighth, second, and third day of the warm disease, the body becomes fully heated; the neck fills with pain and the membrane is affected by food.

When vomiting occurs with a thin, taut pulse, by the seventh day it changes; after ten to eleven days the warm disease is established; sweating occurs; by eight to nine days the condition becomes fully apparent with head pain.

When the patient reaches the point of death with cold reversal (jue), the pulse is firm and tight; sweating spontaneously occurs by the seventh day; the pulse remains firm and forceful; in urgent cases the patient sweats; in deficiency cases soft sweating occurs; such patients do not die.

translation:
Methods for Treating Epidemic Pestilence (Lùyì Zhìfǎ)

[On pulse and symptoms:] When the pulse is painful — in warm disease, if one uses purgative medicines and the patient is seriously ill with a large, rapid pulse that becomes faint and cut off, this does not necessarily mean death. If the patient is calm, death may still occur. In warm disease, if there is diarrhea with abdominal symptoms, and the pulse reverses, recovery may be difficult.

[General principles:] What is called warm-heat disease refers to conditions that arise before the summer solstice, called warm disease (wēnbìng), and those arising after the summer solstice, called heat disease (rèbìng). When cold turns to spring, one must guard against developing warm-heat illness. When an irregular cold is present and many people fall ill, the treatment should supplement, disperse, and reduce as appropriate. When one person is ill, one uses a moderate reducing approach with Yangming channel medicines.

[On epidemic treatment:] When two or three people are ill with cold-damage patterns, one should use Minor or Major Bupleurum Decoction (Chaihu Tang), adjusting for Yangming-stage treatment. When the illness is widely spread, use Minor or Major Bupleurum Decoction as appropriate, treating through the Yangming channel.

[Seasonal variations:] For epidemics arising in autumn from cold-spring patterns, use Cangzhu (Atractylodes) with Shengma (Cimicifuga) and Danggui (Angelica). For treating exterior-interior half-stage epidemic disorders, use Minor Bupleurum Decoction; for interior patterns, use Major Bupleurum Decoction. For pustular eruptions, use Renzhonghuang Decoction (Human Yellow Decoction). For autumn cold-epidemic warm diseases, begin with Bupleurum preparations.

[Further formulas:] Use Baihu Jieji Tang (White Tiger Muscle-Releasing Decoction) for fever and dryness, adjusting with warming and cooling medicines. For Baidou San (Defeat Toxin Powder) treating half-exterior, half-interior patterns — for interior patterns use Major Bupleurum Decoction; for initial-stage warm disease, examine the day of onset according to yin-yang channel timing and administer accordingly.

[On special epidemic types:] There also exist the conditions known as Datou Zhan (Big-Head Epidemic) and Hamamo Wen (Toad Epidemic swellings). For these, at the initial stage of infection, regardless of which day it began, administer the Nine-Ingredient Notopterygium Decoction (Jiuwei Qianghuo Tang) for effective results.

Citrus peel (橘), Gardenia (梔), Bitter orange (枳殼), Bupleurum (柴胡), Tangerine peel (陳皮), Cyperus (香附子), Atractylodes (蒼朮), Saposhnikovia (防風), Ligusticum (藁本), Licorice (甘草) — each one packet. Add ginger, three sheng of siler, aged tangerine peel, and perilla leaf.

Five Plague Elixir (五瘟丹)

Treats epidemic plague diseases circulating through the population, as well as cold-damage febrile illnesses. For Jiǎ years, which belong to Fire, Coptis (黃連) is the ruling herb. For Fire years it is the ruler. For Yǐ years it is the ruler. For Dīng and Gēng years it is the ruler. Licorice belongs to the nettle/earth category, using the leaves. For Xīn years, one portion is the ruler. For Rén years it is the ruler. For Guǐ years, three liang is used.

Simmer fragrant ramie (香苧) in strong decoction, add it after straining; combine with fresh ginger, process together until a paste forms, then make pills the size of a marble. Coat with cinnabar and fine-grained rhubarb powder.

Coat the pills, and also treat the gate (i.e., the mouth/throat) during seasonal epidemic; apply gold-leaf patch, use water to nourish and promote sleep.

Lǔ Chen Pills (鹵陳九)

Treats the four-wind seasonal qi epidemic diseases, as well as the five types of jaundice-plague, warm-heat illness, namely the yellow [fever type].

Rén Zhōng Huáng Pills (人中黃九) [Processed human bile/yellow]

Use dried powder, medicated leaven (神麴), four-substance paste, mix and form pills. For each dose use Aconite (附子), Coptis (黃連), Scutellaria (黃苓), seven to ten pills each; Scutellaria and other herbs divided, with Platycodon (桔梗), Atractylodes (蒼朮), processed as a ginseng decoction.

Cinnabar and realgar are used as a coating. One may also use red decoction to swallow the pills down. If Rén Zhōng Huáng is unavailable — [text continues on next page].

translation:
Ruyi Dan (As-You-Wish Elixir)

Specially treats epidemic pestilence, miasmic qi, yang disorders, all manner of corpse-ghost afflictions, miasma poisoning, and accidental toxin ingestion.

Ingredients include: iron filings, gold, mineral substances, Wu (Sichuan) aconite, various unprepared herbs, coins [copper], five-portion, eight-portion [measurements], blast-fried [preparations], eight coins of purple [herbs], imperial dispensary-grade human [musk/ingredients].

Ginseng, cinnamon bark, bupleurum, Sichuan aconite, poria, five portions each, tiger [bone] coins, eight coins of coptis, purple [herb] coins, magnolia bark, human [musk].

Right: Select an auspicious day, grind finely, form into pills, use as follows for treating febrile disease with surging pulse, high fever and accumulation.

Hei Nu Jiu (Black Slave Pills)

Used to treat conditions where yang ming (stomach meridian) evil heat causes the four limbs to be affected, with membrane involvement, the pathogen moving inward and spreading.

Da Tou Chuang Zheng (Large-Head Sore Syndrome)

This refers to epidemic evil qi accumulating to form large swellings of the head, resembling lesser yang excess heat, with evil qi causing cracking of membranes, involving pestilential conditions.

The condition known as large-head disease mostly arises from evil qi accumulating in the head, with intense yang ming (stomach meridian) heat, causing massive swelling. Most cases arise from epidemic seasonal pestilence spreading widely.

Also called "thunder-head wind" (Lei Tou Feng); its symptoms are painful swelling of the head and face, often fatal. One should analyze the movement of seasonal qi. The throat and pharynx are also affected.

Large-head pestilence with head swelling arises from epidemic pestilence spreading through the population.

大頭瘟治法

噫塞堵寒害人最速冬温後多有此病之門。乃大頭瘟也。

根令其候發時毒初面發熱頭耳痛咽喉體赤腫甚無者恍惚或結核有能救者頭項腫。

兩目。陽異面腦腫後陽下明防腫也走耳前後太陽并額表面。陽也謹護。

多者防毒散。炒裏微識多下者防風通聖散。服仰叩加護。

使藥之上法東微治。炒當先普濟消毒飲。子服緩最妙者邪人見中。

於次及彼門行。急緩後徐徐急服。有寒質藥是。

則無形之處。當是高之分後宜。急緩者用邪氣。蘇八中熱氣有形在。

浸酒。上為此地。切客勿當降邪去。炒妙也。大頭酒此熱氣中有形在。

大瘟若俗之謂時毒不可。鼻内搗藥三。不可治也。如毒氣出農取血十者。

治之必看病之日人月日。寬日藥五次藥以之。必不傳染是此良藥。

法在必治之作大瘟數俗之謂時毒不時用重毒者三。可治也。
translation:
Treatment Methods for Epidemic Great Head Swelling (Datou Wen)

This disease spreads extremely fast. It occurs frequently after warm winters. This is the illness known as Datou Wen (Great Head Epidemic).

The initial symptoms include fever of the face, pain in the head and ears, sore throat, redness and severe swelling of the body. Some patients become confused or develop lumps. In serious cases, the head and neck swell enormously.

Both eyes are affected. Swelling appears on the face, brain region, and behind the ears. It spreads along the front and back of the taiyang (greater yang) channel, across the forehead and face. One must carefully protect these areas.

For severe cases, use Fang Du San (Toxin-Dispersing Powder), stir-fried. For those with downward symptoms, use Fang Feng Tong Sheng San (Ledebouriella Sage-Inspired Powder).

The primary treatment method is Pu Ji Xiao Du Yin (Universal Benefit Toxin-Eliminating Decoction). Administer gradually and repeatedly for best results.

For cases with cold constitution, use appropriate warming medicines accordingly.

The treatment must be adapted based on whether the pathogenic qi has taken form or remains formless. Internally, stir-fried medicines and medicated wines may be used.

For what is commonly called epidemic toxic swelling: if the interior of the nose is pounded and medicine is applied three times without improvement, the condition may be beyond treatment. One may attempt to extract blood from the affected area.

Treatment must be monitored daily. Administer medicine five times per day cycle. If this regimen is followed, transmission and contagion can be prevented. This is an excellent formula.

translation:
Pujeui Soktok Eumja (Universal Relief Toxin-Dispersing Drink)

For cases where, within three to four days, the condition has not resolved, it is appropriate to use Hyungbang Paedok-san (Schizonepeta and Ledebouriella Powder to Overcome Toxins). From the seventh to eighth day, if the head and face have not resolved, one should use [the following formula]. If there is blockage and obstruction [of passages], and redness persists for ten or more days, [special treatment is indicated]. If the patient cannot taste food, death is likely. Burdock seed (Niúbàng), thistle, and closure of the throat and larynx with loss of voice should be treated [accordingly]. Toxin-dispersing drinks, bitter preparations, Sagebrush Powder, and formulas for spreading heavenly epidemic conditions affecting the head — for the great-head plague with qi leaking to the head: Huang Lu Plague Formula, Two-Yellow Decoction to Relieve Toxins, Toxin-Dispersing Decoction, and Toxin-Dispersing Pill.

[Preparation:] On the first day, send [the medicine at the appointed time], or administer orally. Add Fangfeng (Ledebouriella) 1 qian, Bohe (Peppermint) half [qian], Gancao (Licorice) divided portions, Mabo (Puffball) 3 pieces, Banlangen (Isatis root) ground into powder, Danggui, Huangqin (Scutellaria) and Huanglian (Coptis) both dry-fried, Lianqiao (Forsythia), Chaihu (Bupleurum) each portion. Mix with water; if convulsions are severe and there is stagnation, bloodletting may be indicated. In the fourth month, epidemics were widespread; initially the swelling was severe.

The qi of the earth caused many deaths. All patients experienced nausea, throat swelling, heaviness of the body, dry mouth — commonly called "Big Head Heavenly Epidemic." This formula was devised to counter it and named the Universal Relief Toxin-Dispersing Drink. Upon taking it, the head and face all recovered.

This formula is from the physician Tan Zhixian, said to have been composed by a heavenly immortal.
Engraved on stone and distributed, it is said to treat epidemic outbreaks, severe sores, and swelling and pain of the face. Large yellow (rhubarb), wine-prepared.

Haedok-tang (Decoction to Resolve Toxin)
Divide and roughly cut: Bupleurum, Coptis (Huanglian), Forsythia (Lianqiao), Scutellaria (Huangqin), Angelica body, Forsythia, Platycodon, Licorice — each one qian. Large yellow (rhubarb), wine-prepared.
Decoct. Treats epidemic sores, redness and swelling of the face and neck with pain.

Belamcanda (Shegan), Angelica dahurica (Baizhi), Licorice — each, in portions. Treats smallpox, with Ligusticum (Chuanxiong). Boil, add bamboo juice, ginger three slices, adjust with water. Take orally. Ledebouriella (Fangfeng), Notopterygium (Qianghuo) — applied. Treats accumulated heat with Coptis, Scutellaria, Forsythia, rhubarb decocted, stone-washed. Take two qian.

Niubang Qinlian Tang (Decoction with Burdock, Scutellaria, and Coptis)
Forsythia, Scrophularia (Xuanshen), Licorice — each portion simmered and steamed with wine; large rhubarb, washed with stone, decocted, take two qian adjusted in water.
Fangfeng, Qianghuo — each, as needed.

Pianlu San (Powder of Reed/Duckweed)
Two liang: Reed (Lu), sliced and dried, ground into powder. Scrophularia — take three doses each. Two liang, swelling of throat, hemp seed, pig's bile, Scutellaria — each as needed.

Erhuang Tang (Two-Yellow Decoction)
Water decoction. Start with small doses, taken warm. Coptis (Huanglian), soaked in wine, stir-fried; large rhubarb (Dahuang), Licorice (Gancao), raw — each in portions.

Contagion spreads through the nose, settles in the sinuses, and causes sweating; realgar, when applied [destroys the miasma] and thus prevents contagion. Therefore the Shenghui Lun states: exhaled qi travels throughout and agitates the qi.

translation:
Symptoms of Demonic Affliction (邪崇形證)

When one's faculties of sight, hearing, speech, and action are deficient, and one speaks wildly and babbles incoherently, this is called demonic affliction (邪崇). It is said that the blood's vital spirit can manifest in extreme speech. It resembles epilepsy but is not true epilepsy; the fire flares at times, and malevolent spirits invade the qi, causing spirit-illness or demonic possession in the body.

Signs include: forms resembling madness but not madness; nighttime moaning; spontaneous laughing; self-urging; apparent deep sleep; sudden clarity; at times, no medicine or needling can help; the person is startled; they become possessed; defiled objects afflict the body.

In songs, the person sings sorrowfully; they are fond of music but cannot eat or drink; they speak of ghosts and spirits; they seem to sit as though confined in a cage; no medicine or needles are effective.

The mei-demon causes grief and sorrow; the di-demon causes love of beautiful sounds; the heart aches; the person converses with ghosts and spirits; they drift as if there is no way out; they sit as if enclosed; no medicine or needles help.

Ten Zhu Conditions and Five Corpse Conditions (十疰五尸)

Zhu means: a condition that lodges and accumulates. The ten zhu conditions are: qi-zhu, which lingers and transfers the pathogenic influence. It is said the qi travels outside, and the spirit wanders, generating fear and evil, causing the vital qi to become deficient; the essence is as if drunk; the spirit drifts away.

The zhu condition causes the illness to linger, passing easily from the dying to the living nearby. [Needle treatment indicated.]

The sinking, heavy pulse that stops — four kinds of people: those who act like Dong in regulating the pulse; the pulse may also be scattered, rushing, fine, bundled, and slow.

The spirit is confused, the mind disordered, mixed with demonic influences. The pulse alternates between large, flooding, exuberant, small, large, long, short, rapid, slow, knotted — all these pulse types are relevant.

translation:
Origins of Carbuncles and Abscesses (Yongju / 癰疽)

On Carbuncles and Abscesses:

One medical discussion states: What is called a carbuncle (yong) arises when cold qi accumulates in the flesh, generating swelling and pain. This is because cold qi holds the qi in a state of deficiency, and the swelling of the wind-emperor (a classical metaphor) constitutes what is called a carbuncle.

Another medical discussion states: A carbuncle arises when cold qi fails to flow freely through the interstices of the flesh, giving rise to swollen masses. The liver swelling and stomach swelling can shift location.

When asked how this comes about: It is said that when [the defensive qi] stagnates and ceases to flow, the great bones suffer stagnation, and the swelling accumulates; when the imperial qi is blocked, the blood overflows.

When the heat is great and unrelenting, it is said that stagnation and failure to flow leads to rotting of the flesh; when the flesh decays and cannot circulate, it rots and injures, and this is called a carbuncle (yong).

When the muscle heat is extreme and does not cease, the heat overcomes and scorches; the five [types of stagnation] do not rot into decay and injury, and this too is called a carbuncle (yong).

[The following section describes moxibustion points and methods:]

On the left and right sides: apply moxibustion. For the nose and qi on the right cheek, tilt the head. Various points on either side. Seven cones of moxa on both sides. 七十一
translation:
Signs That a Carbuncle or Abscess (Yongju) Is About to Develop

When heat-qi accumulates and becomes intense, if without apparent cause the muscles, sinews, and network vessels beneath the skin become affected, and the six bowels and five viscera lose their harmony, then qi stagnates and binds in the sinews. This can occur along the foot taiyang vessel, causing abscesses in the bones and sinews.

It is also said: When the three yang develop illness, the result is carbuncles and abscesses. The three yang governs the bands of circulation. Blood moves within the vessels, while coarse qi moves on the exterior; when yang strikes against the kidney, blood accumulates; when the yin band is involved, blood moves through the vessels, and blood and fluids become thick and turbid, turning into fire-qi that moves inward, resulting in carbuncles and abscesses.

When pathogenic influences accumulate, they permeate inward into the eight vessels, sometimes overflowing and sometimes binding; blood fluids become thick, fire-qi moves inward and outward, forming internal and external carbuncles.

When the six bowels are affected, yang becomes excessive, generating outward eruptions; when heat and swelling burst outward, the root of the abscess is exposed. If yin is affected, blood surges violently. Where the skin and muscles dry up and become rigid, this indicates deep-seated disease in the five viscera. Where the swelling is soft and large, with the flesh moist and hot and bloated, this indicates disease in the six bowels.

In general, persistent fever and chills with no relief, restlessness, thirst, and prolonged illness over many years — all of these are signs that carbuncles and abscesses are about to develop, and their qi presses urgently.

72
translation:
Names and Appearances of Carbuncles and Ulcers (Yong and Ju)

Many people suffer from carbuncles and ulcers (yong-ju). Some endure this illness without treatment. It is said that the seven emotions, when harbored for a long time, are among the most harmful, and one must attend to this.

It is said: When there is slight warmth, eruption is imminent; one knows the carbuncle is forming. When the pulse is in the channels, the eruption will spread throughout the body without a specific form. Black ulcers (ju) tend to develop internally; the reverse indicates something lodged within.

When qi becomes knotted it forms a carbuncle (yong), though there may be no pain at first. As the classics say: when the emotions harbor stagnation over time, and blood stagnates together without moving, carbuncles and ulcers will erupt in the body. Black ulcers tend to develop internally, while reversal indicates failure of circulation.

Many carbuncles arise; the decoction of honeysuckle herb (wintersweet tea) is often the best treatment. One must address blood stagnation when there is confusion and blockage, removing the obstruction and guiding the will and vital energy.

One chi in size is called ju (deep ulcer); two chi is called yong (surface carbuncle). Sizes ranging from two chi down to two cun, and up to five cun, are classified as yong (carbuncle). Those smaller remain unruptured.

The Causes of Swelling, Pain, and Itching of Carbuncles and Ulcers

It is said that carbuncles and ulcers arise solely because yang qi overcomes internally, causing heat. When intense heat prevails and erupts suddenly, swelling arises severely.

Those presenting with a small head like a millet grain are classified as papular eruptions. At most they do not exceed two or three cun in size. In women, these are heat carbuncles arising on the skin surface.

The same type: small millet-like heads, papular eruptions, not exceeding two or three cun. In women these are heat carbuncles arising on the skin.

Ranging from one to five cun in depth, with floating swelling and a rounded root, small and red ones are yong (carbuncles); those up to eight cun are ju (deep ulcers). After one cun, heat develops, erupting on the skin surface, with color changes and pale redness.

When there is severe pain in the hand area, with spasms and eruptions, occurring in the spaces between joints, or arising with irritability, located around the navel area, with color changes and pale appearance.

If the color turns purple-black, hard and firm upon eruption, or if it becomes deeply sunken, the body shows multiple recurring eruptions that keep appearing.

translation:
Distinguishing the Severity and Depth of Carbuncles and Abscesses

A carbuncle (yong) has skin above it that is thin and glossy; an abscess (ju) has skin above it that is rough — these are the distinguishing signs.

When a carbuncle arises deep, it becomes a deficiency-type pain. This does not mean absolute deficiency, but rather refers to intense heat with the flesh wasting subtly, causing one not to recognize the pain at the affected area.

When a carbuncle forms with bound swelling, pathogenic wind and cold bind internally; when heat is excessive it immediately produces no pus head — pain and swelling arise together, reaching their peak at once.

When heat is extreme and is caused by alternating cold and heat, toxin-qi flares and moves through the channels and collaterals, all driven by fire. When heat-toxin spreads broadly, it causes blood to stagnate and not flow. When there is heat, the affected person experiences soreness and distension near the lesion with microscopic changes.

When the core forms, the lesion becomes red and inflamed; swelling appears, large in size, arising from wind-cold. The skin surface becomes elevated and swollen; the color is hard and thick due to heat-toxin. The lesion may or may not be painful.

When toxin-qi contacts and injures, it is appropriate to resolve wind and pain. When qi forces the blood, pain is inevitable; it must gradually diminish. If the opposite occurs, the pain increases.

When pus forms, the qi spreads, the swelling retreats, the skin relaxes and opens, and the pain must gradually decrease. If the contrary occurs, the pain intensifies.

In general, for the condition of carbuncles and abscesses, the pain manifests in many ways according to the pattern of qi and flesh involvement, with heat-toxin steaming inward — these are the essential signs of carbuncles and abscesses.

translation:
On carbuncles and abscesses: When the pulse is deficient, one should not use draining or attacking methods on the interior. When the pulse ultimately does not develop along the five viscera and the viscera ultimately do not erupt, one becomes confused; correct treatment calls for internally generated heat, where the heat-evil lodges in the bones.

On the qi and blood: If yang [energy] is not carefully managed from the initial onset, when the flesh color turns red-purple, this condition, though feverish and greatly swollen, will inevitably produce many complications. translation:
Determining the Fatal Locations of Carbuncles and Abscesses

The body has five regions. The front (prostrate position): the rabbit area — first, the dorsum of the foot — second; those who have carbuncles and abscesses on the back — third.

Locations where [carbuncles] are fatal and cannot be cured: sores erupting at the temples — fourth; a high swelling at the dangerous area; this area is near the rear of the cheekbone, at the perineal root.

All [carbuncles] above the pubic hairline, in the lower abdomen, at the wind points, the seven dangerous points, behind the eyes — these are high-danger locations where carbuncles and abscesses are inevitably fatal, at the root of the perineum.

Eruptions due to [disease in] the lower abdomen affecting the water passages, coccyx, and bone formations; ear, joint bones, front and rear near the cheekbone area, and the perineal root.

All malignant eruptions at the nose, mouth, eyebrows, face, the palace region, called the "eye region," extending to the fifth [point], down to the lower landscape, to the groin near the rear cheekbone area.

Eruptions in women: carbuncles and sores at the five points — erupting on the abdomen, back, and spine; from behind the eye to the fifth and ninth landscape points, the inner shin, thigh, and popliteal fossa.

Carbuncles erupting in the sheath and chest; knowing the swelling and edema of the face, the back, the eyes, inner shin, the four regions of the thighs, shins, and popliteal fossa.

Or from fatigue and excess alcohol, the qi becomes thick and toxic; the pulse at the head and flesh, when thunder-like eruptions arise in the visceral palaces such as the Central Palace, the Great Gate, and the Hidden [regions] — these are internal carbuncles.

Or phlegm and stagnant qi cause painful abscesses internally; when the five points in the head erupt and the hidden fire in the organs overwhelms everything, these are all carbuncles and abscesses — one type is the great lip-and-brain popliteal carbuncle on the back.

Carbuncles and Abscesses Must Be Distinguished as Internal or External

Heart-region carbuncles: the lung-kidney carbuncles that occur after this, following the great critical period. Stomach duct and intestinal carbuncles are internal; those of the Triple Burner, Kidney, Upper [region], Heaven, Sun — these are lung carbuncles when the signs appear on the corresponding day.

[Organ correspondences:] Heart, Gate of the Mind, Open Source, Liver, Small Intestine, Stomach Gate, Triple Burner, Kidney Upper, Heaven.

translation:
Abscesses and Carbuncles Should Be Differentiated by Their Meridians

Occurring daily: brain abscess, back abscess, temple abscess, eyebrow abscess, cheekbone abscess, jaw abscess, breast abscess, axillary abscess, penetrating abscess.

The Governor Vessel and abscesses/carbuncles; Foot Taiyang Meridian abscesses; Foot Shaoyang Meridian abscesses; Hand Taiyang Meridian abscesses; Foot Yangming Meridian abscesses; Hand Yangming Meridian abscesses; Foot Shaoyang Meridian abscesses; Hand Shaoyang Meridian abscesses; Foot Taiyin Meridian abscesses; Hand Taiyin Meridian abscesses.

Yang fu abscesses and carbuncles arise from the exterior yang meridians — the three yang vessels: Foot Yangming, Foot Taiyang, Foot Shaoyang, and the inner yin vessels of the Foot Yangming.

Abscess pulse: When there is heat and swelling in the pulse, at times carbuncles and malignant sores arise. A rapid pulse with fever in both limbs and numbness — this is a yang condition.

Using this [understanding]: if one does not know about the blood — how can one safely expel toxins, reduce swelling, benefit the flesh, and heal sores? Over a long time, one should manage and prevent [these conditions] with care. It is essential to do so.

Regarding the amount of blood: the yin meridians — along the pathways connecting to the head vessels — the foot yin, Yangming, hand three yin and yang, through the Governor and Conception vessels, and the foot three Yangming vessels.
