77
translation:
Difficult-to-Treat and Untreatable Patterns of Carbuncles and Deep Abscesses (Yong-ju)

When the pulse of the lungs and liver is neither soft nor rapid, and a yin-type abscess arises on a yang channel: if the pulse is wiry and flooding and persists in tension, it will develop into a carbuncle; if the flooding pulse becomes stagnant in the yin aspect, the pulse will become fine and sunken.

When a deep abscess fails to express toxin outward, this is a yin abscess occurring on a yang channel. The pulse should be distinguished: if there is a floating, flooding, and stagnant-clear pulse internally, this belongs to the yang category — this is the first indicator.

When an abscess fills and there is sunken, accumulating pulse with bodily heat, and the flesh shows no heat but the pulse is rapid, the body without heat — in such cases pus has formed internally. When the main center has pus, the carbuncle swells and accumulates pus, causing surrounding pain. When the pulse is slippery and rapid with accumulation, there is no gathering, and the body is feverish; heat disperses as the pulse becomes rapid — in this case pus has developed with heat. When the pulse becomes flooding and excessive, the pus is large and copious, making it difficult to treat. This covers nine overlapping pain patterns. First indicator.

When a carbuncle first erupts as a swelling that is high and prominent, it is easy to treat. But if the toxin erupts shallowly, resembling millet grains, it is shallow.

When many patients suffer from lung heat with blood discharge, and the condition is large — the world regards this as a difficult pattern — if the pus is hot and the pulse is flooding and dispersed, and the lung heat fails to resolve, it is difficult to treat.

If the pulse is flooding and the discharge is fresh-looking, it is difficult to contain, and the toxin makes the pus difficult to resolve. If the pulse pattern shows only yang without balance, it is a difficult pattern; when the carbuncle pulse arrives stagnant with vexation and stasis, and a flooding lung-dispersing pulse is seen, treatment of this condition is extremely difficult to bring to full resolution.

When the lesion breaks and its granules are like bean-sized fragments, level with the surrounding flesh, or shows redness internally; at times itchy — on no account should one treat it in the early stage as if it were a superficial yellow pustule.

In treatment: if from the beginning the abscess does not mature, becomes greatly painful, and the pain is low and sunken; if it erupts outwardly it is difficult; if it erupts inwardly it is like a fish scale pattern internally — these are all difficult to treat.

後。內闌。常。人白無時喜笑。不痛乃如內癰。病者抻病深深。內氣拳縮病深用乃榮癰不軟。者病口小。

按腫之軟。按之堅硬半軟半硬謂有膿也按之強而不即復痛者有無肌膿者膿者以膿熱不者以為無。

translation:
Judging Whether an Abscess (Yong-Ju) Has Pus, and Whether It Is Superficial or Deep

Concerning carbuncles and deep abscesses (yong-ju): those that are difficult to treat may be fatal. Those categorized as yang-type swellings, associated with the six fu organs, are generally easier to treat. Those of the ju (deep abscess) type are harder to treat.

Regarding depth: if the area is deep and the disease has spread inward, the mass is hard as stone, pus forms deep within, and the swelling does not soften, small plasters and medicines may be applied to the opening.

Regarding internal signs: if the person shows no pain but laughs and smiles frequently, this may indicate an internal abscess. When the disease is deep, the qi becomes contracted and constricted within.

Regarding the appearance of blood: if fresh blood emerges easily, or dark blood appears, this indicates vacuity. If there is pathogenic heat with deep-seated pus, and no pus can be expressed by hand pressure, pus is still present.

Regarding palpation to determine pus: press the swelling — if it is soft, then press firmly; if it is half-soft and half-hard, this indicates pus is present. If pressing firmly causes pain that does not immediately rebound, there may be pus present mixed within the flesh.

Regarding shallow versus deep palpation: light pressure that causes immediate rebound pain indicates shallow pus. If pressing halfway down finds the mass half-soft and half-hard on all four sides, pus is present within the flesh.

If the area feels like water under pressure and rebounds immediately upon removal of the hand, there is pus. If pressing causes no heat and the area remains soft, there is no pus.

If the patient with a carbuncle or deep abscess develops alternating chills and fever, thirst, and the swelling does not resolve over a long period, this is a serious sign.

translation:
Carbuncles and Furuncles: The Spreading Halo (Aura)

When the facial color turns sallow and yellow, it means heat is steaming upward and a carbuncle-sore has already formed — this is fire. Heat causes the blood to become stagnant and the flesh to rot. When the defensive qi moves and a carbuncle forms, the presence of pus water indicates it is on the verge of transformation. Just as ripe fruit and lush vegetables signal ripeness, so too does blood transform into pus. Turbid water indicates swelling; hard pus indicates the water of corruption; when the flesh rots, it is separated from the nutritive qi.

When the discharge is thick and turbid, the swollen flesh has not yet liquefied. When the pus is thin, the body has not yet been able to produce true pus, and thus cannot expel it. White discharge indicates that true pus has not yet formed — this is not a halo sign, and the patient may survive. With three halos it is still manageable; after four halos, if a jade-white halo appears, the prognosis is fatal.

When two carbuncles are present on either side of the mouth, and a red halo appears, with up to three such halos the patient may still survive; with four halos it is still possible; but if a jade halo appears, it is fatal.

One to three red halos: survivable. Four halos or more: if a jade halo is seen, it is fatal. This is extremely difficult to treat medically; once it has formed in the abdominal region, it becomes very large and the surrounding tissue turns red and moist.

Fatal Signs of Carbuncles and Furuncles

If more than ten days pass without urgent treatment, death follows. When heat erupts at the head with no treatment possible, and the yang qi descends, the qi penetrates the abdomen, affecting the anterior channel and the liver and lung meridians. After seven days the abdominal tissue rots — this is a fatal sign. When it resembles a large iron bean, called "smoke-heart," it cannot be treated; it descends into the abdomen, and within seven days the intestines rot — a fatal sign.

A carbuncle arising at the navel region is called "sweet carbuncle" (甘疽); its color is greenish and shaped like a trichosanthes fruit; the patient constantly suffers alternating chills and fever. If not treated urgently, death follows within ten years; afterward pus will discharge. A carbuncle arising at the coccyx region is called "sharp carbuncle" (銳疽).

translation:
Methods for Treating Carbuncles and Abscesses (Yong-ju)

The following signs indicate the nine malignant conditions: the lips turn blue and curl back, the face turns black, the stool becomes foul and white, and the eyes show abnormal changes. These are among the nine unfavorable signs and three auspicious signs.

When swallowing is difficult, it indicates obstruction. When there is severe pain, coughing, and the skin peels, these relate to the five pathways. If the jade [vital energy] flows in reverse, the neck area becomes disordered, and defecation is irregular, the prognosis is unfavorable.

When there is hoarseness, deafness, internal blockage, difficulty speaking, the face sinks, sweating appears without cause, and vision becomes impaired, these are all serious indicators.

In the early stages, when pathogenic [evil] qi begins to manifest, the ancient method is to supplement internally and fill the interior to expel the pus, then once the pus is gone, new muscle tissue will form to close the wound membrane.

When the abscess begins to spread, apply moxibustion externally to draw out the poison and fill the interior. If fire moxibustion is used properly, it will disperse the condition.

For deep-seated abscesses, use fire and moxibustion to draw the pathogen outward and fill the interior back toward a favorable outcome.

For abscesses located in the viscera and bowels, do not apply fire directly. Use the methods of supplementing and filling the interior.

For large internal abscesses, the root of the pathogen must be cut off. Use dispersing formulas, and divide the interior treatment with cinnabar-based prescriptions.

Overall, the urgent treatment is to administer the Five Fragrance and Forsythia Decoction (Wuxiang Lianqiao Tang) to circulate through the channels. First distinguish whether the pathogenic evil is excess or deficient, and treat accordingly with warming agents.

For the treatment of carbuncles and abscesses in both the young and the elderly at the initial onset, Five Fragrance and Forsythia Decoction is urgently required.

Page 84 — Formulas for Treating Carbuncles, Swellings, and Toxic Sores

**Five-Fragrance Forsythia Decoction (五香連翹湯)**
Treats carbuncles, abscesses, scrofula (lumps in the neck), and all toxic swellings. Cut all ingredients into pieces: Agastache (Huoxiang), Aquilaria wood (Muxiang), Cloves (Dingxiang), Licorice (Gancao), Schizonepeta (Shegan), Frankincense (Duxiang), Forsythia (Lianqiao), Job's tears (Yiyi), Scutellaria (Huangqin), Gardenia (Zhizi), Aquilaria (Muxiang), Angelica (Baizhi) — each measured in portions — with Cimicifuga (Shengma), Mirabilite (Mangxiao) each one portion. Decoct in water and take orally. Also facilitates qi circulation, resolves blood stagnation; for cases with difficult urination and constipation, add to the decoction.

**Five-Benefit Rhubarb Decoction (五利大黃湯)**
Decoct two qian in water; take in two doses. Treats all manner of malignant sores and toxic swellings. Rhubarb (Dahuang) — suitable for young children, each dose one serving. Ingredients include: Adzuki beans, Adzuki bean skin, Alisma (Zexie), Frankincense (separately ground), Myrrh soaked in vinegar — each separately ground, each one dose serving.

**Detoxification Pill (化毒丹)**
Harmonized into pills. Treats carbuncles and abscesses. Ingredients like a soybean in size; after a long period, when one wishes to consolidate with these pills: Frankincense, Myrrh soaked in vinegar — each separately ground, seven portions; also grind two portions of Myrrh soaked in vinegar; Cyperus grass, ground fine; Donkey-dung leaven — paste into pills with flour paste.

**Expel and Consolidate Powder (托裏散)**
All herbs cut into pieces, combined. Two and a half qian per dose, decocted in water, take one qian. Treats carbuncles and abscesses, swellings after surgery, prolonged non-healing wounds. When one wishes to supplement with this formula: Angelica (Danggui), Rehmannia (Dihuang), Rehmannia (Baijiang), Angelica root (Baizhi), Ginseng (Renshen), Licorice (Gancao), Poria (Fuling), Astragalus (Huangqi) — each one qian; Notopterygium (Muxiang) — for painless cases, one qian and two portions.

**Coptis Detoxification Powder (黃連消毒散)**
Treats carbuncles and abscesses, back swellings, toxic sores with suppuration. Coptis (Huanglian), Notopterygium (Qianghuo), Siler (Fangfeng), Forsythia (Lianqiao), Job's tears (Yiyi), Scutellaria (Huangqin), Gardenia (Zhizi), Platycodon (Jiegeng) — each seven fen; Ginseng (Renshen), Licorice (Gancao), Rehmannia (Dihuang), Anemarrhena (Zhimu) — each five fen. Also: Astragalus (Huangqi), Notopterygium (Huo) — each one qian and two portions (for pain).

When toxin sinks inward into the organs and bowels, one must first support the stomach, strengthen the qi, and cause the channels and collaterals [to carry the toxin outward].

When the mouth of the sore will not close and there is internal heat with the toxin invading inward from the root, if the evidence is deep one must restore to the surface technique — if excessive dampness appears, remove the floating dampness.

Supporting Decoction; Immortal Transmission Detoxify Powder; Thousand Flower Decoction; Interior Supporting Coptis Decoction; Benefiting Qi Powder; if the pattern is not clear and has been long-standing, it is appropriate to support the interior — for those in whom pus and blood have not yet formed.

癰疽五發證

發腦、發鬢、發眉、發頤、發心，是為五發，至險。為氣急抱寧，脈急至陰。

玉香散，其證發腦，發鬢，發眉痛惡，是為五發。有是為氣急抱至險。

得破八急在大膜鑽上入腦，錢際生起，為癰疽痘爛，皮破穴，起之易腦。

急發毒內破出方可。初皮厚色，難得破穴，如難破皮癰，須破之。

黑廣如發顏稜亦為發眉重，鼻人有氣分下。顧發為左是青同皆。

石為顏稜日發，亦為老大硬，左右見額膜角翕，及太陽穴右。生實，如皆同。

發、亦重眉，背源下人中及顧發，為左是。

是為烽煙風氣則有三種，有食氣癒寒有瘡。發為左是青同皆生。

有毒則發，食之則癒發有瘡，寒有氣場則發，為四種氣場，因內外食氣多風。

二熟香藥毒有發，則毒堅硬腫狀，狗風三損，則不難復，內外煎藥因敞方。房。不宜因七服宜。

黃甘散，宜散連翹獨散，毒散。二者不內，毒發如石淫不宜。因國。宜七。

情宜老膏老宜速志，酒翹獨勝散，毒散。

宜膏梔花，金石藥，世弱硬如，衛石淫不，腎氣九痛。

處重，着豆，湯如紡石，觀不可。用五發，證欲腫作痛，煩腎氣溺引。

translation:
The Five Manifestations of Carbuncle and Abscess (癰疽五發證)

The five manifestations are: eruption at the head/brain, eruption at the temples, eruption at the eyebrows, eruption at the jaw/cheek, and eruption at the chest/heart. These are called the Five Manifestations and are extremely dangerous conditions. They arise from urgent qi obstruction, with the pulse rapid and reaching to the yin level.

Yu Xiang San (Jade Fragrance Powder): The symptoms include eruption at the brain, eruption at the temples, eruption at the eyebrows with severe pain. These constitute the Five Manifestations, which are characterized by urgent qi and are extremely dangerous.

When toxicity penetrates the inner membrane and bores into the brain, forming layers, it gives rise to carbuncles and ulcerated pustules. If the skin breaks and opens at the hole, recovery becomes easier.

In acute onset, the toxin must break through from inside out. Initially the skin is thick and discolored, making it difficult for the abscess to break through. If it cannot break through the skin, one must lance and open it.

If the eruption appears black and widespread at the face and along the ridge, and also erupts at the eyebrows with severe swelling, affecting the nose and people experiencing qi descent — all should be observed together.

At the stone ridge, as eruptions appear daily, they become old, large, and hard. Left and right temples and forehead membranes are affected, along with the Taiyang (temple) acupoint on the right side.

There are three types related to heat qi: wind-type, food-type, and cold-type, each causing ulceration. All belong to the left-side eruption pattern where the condition spreads similarly.

When toxins erupt, consuming food may heal the eruptions, while cold qi conditions cause them to erupt again — these are the four types of qi scenarios, arising from internal and external food qi and wind factors.

When twice-heated aromatic medicinals with toxin-clearing properties are applied, hard swollen masses form. Wind damage causes secondary injury, and recovery from internal and external decoctions depends on appropriate administration. The room should not be cold; seven doses should be taken appropriately.

Huang Gan San (Yellow Licorice Powder): Disperse with Forsythia (Lianqiao) and dispersing agents alone; disperse the toxin. If toxin has penetrated as deep as stone-like hardness, internal administration is not appropriate.

For the aged with cream/ointment preparations, quickly resolve the condition; use wine-prepared Forsythia, alone to overcome and disperse the toxin.

Suitable ointments include Gardenia flower, mineral medicinals — for those who are weak yet with hard masses, protect kidney qi and relieve pain.

In severe cases, with swelling like bean-sized nodes, as in Tang (decoction) formulas involving alum — observe carefully. For the Five Manifestation conditions presenting with swelling, pain, irritability, kidney qi deficiency, and urinary disturbance.

[Marginal notes:] Apply a small amount repeatedly, grinding each time; it harms malignant flesh only, not healthy tissue. For conditions with malignant interior tissue: use a paste combining mulberry bark, with croton seed and realgar added.

On treating sores on the abdomen and back: inject with herbal decoction using hemp; for sores on the four limbs, use bathing powder, and for festering sores, use the cleansing herbal wash.

Warm the medicinal decoction, wash the affected area; eliminate wind and evil qi; decoct ten portions, adding peony; remove the herbal dregs from the pig trotter wash water; reduce to three sheng, bring to a boil.

Ingredients: Dried atractylodes, medicinal herbs, rhubarb, white angelica root, poria, dong quai, notopterygium, two qian each; cypress bark,택란 (Lycopus), licorice, chrysanthemum, schizonepeta, red peony; wash with scallion whites, five portions.

For pain and swelling, this formula, also known by one name, is used by the physician; wash thoroughly until warm and clean; soak until the festering is resolved.

Detoxifying Wash Decoction

Method for Applying Poultices to Carbuncles and Boils

Detoxifying Wash Decoction: For all types of carbuncles and swellings. Sophora root, Schizonepeta, Ledebouriella, Honeybee nest, Licorice — 2 qian each, half a qian. Boil, take the concentrated liquid, wash with it. Do this twice daily; the blood will gradually normalize and warm.

Dried Mugwort Decoction: For tidal sores. Apply white resin plaster over the mouth of the wound, stopping the stagnation. Combine with aged meat and white medicinals; simmer the pus-juice to a concentrate, take a small amount twice daily. This regulates qi and blood, and warms.

Shen Xi Yi Gao (Miraculous Strange Ointment): Apply with fragrant smoke fumigation to difficult-to-treat sores.

Salt-Ash Water: Wash warm. Remove ash. For inflammation of carbuncles and boils, soak in the liquid, wash away blood and fluid, rinse with water.

Mulberry Ash Decoction: Wash twice, warm. Remove residue. For inflammation of carbuncles, boils, and toxic swellings, soak in the liquid, wash away blood, rinse with water.

Method for Applying Poultices to Carbuncles and Boils: In cases of cold or heat, use medicines to subdue the condition. Apply paper or cloth soaked in heated medicinals. Draw out the poison with warmth and heat, to promote healing.

Named medicines may be applied softly over the initial inflammation and toxic swelling using fire-heated preparations to dissolve and disperse.

Round powders applied with iron spatulas on paper, spread on cloth, replaced easily three times; new swellings treated with red-hot medicinals, also for thick swollen skin.

When pus-water appears, wash with medicinal wash. Wait until the mouth of the wound dries, then replace the plaster. For deep lesions, replace easily. Use green-elder ointment with astringent, rich, and aromatic ingredients.

To stop bleeding and drain pus: change the paper dressing daily until healed. It is appropriate to use the Miraculous Ointment — one application, change when yellow fluid appears. If yellow water with borax appears,

Use the yellow powder with ointment. When qi-dryness emerges, apply the ointment. Wait for the dampness to dry from within, then apply clean red plaster. After the wound closes, use the smooth rich ointment.

translation:
Wood Fragrance and Areca Nut Powder

Treats abscesses, ulcers, and sores from which pus and fluid do not stop flowing and flesh does not regenerate. Mix with water to a thick consistency. Ingredients: Wood Fragrance (Muxiang), Areca Nut (Binglang), Phellodendron Bark (Huangbai), Coptis (Huanglian) — equal portions, ground into fine powder, fresh.

Bamboo Tube Method for Drawing Out Toxins

This is suitable for treating all kinds of abscesses, sores, water pox, carbuncles, mature suppurating sores, and various malignant ulcers. Use five tubes or one long tube to draw out the pus and toxins. Apply at the nodes of the bamboo, which is especially effective for hard sores and membranes. Use bamboo tubes — three or five tubes. Apply a paste thickly, then after ten applications the heat will naturally disperse. Use tea bark, cangzhu wood powder, and softened white paste. Chew the bamboo and apply on top; wait until the tube has drawn out the matter. Naturally all the toxins will be expelled.

Distinguishing Internal and External Abscesses and Carbuncles

Those arising within the abdominal membrane are caused by the fire of food and drink, or the fire of the seven emotions affecting the internal organs.

Those located deep within, in the stomach, intestines, or the membrane (huang), are called internal abscesses.

Arm abscess, breast abscess, kidney abscess, stomach abscess, rectal abscess, intestinal abscess, abdominal abscess, perirenal abscess — these are the named types.

Those involving the liver and kidney turning toward the intestines are named dry intestinal and gastric membrane abscesses. Those outside the membrane are called wandering sores and bone abscesses.

點陰膠法

肺癰

內症疳。而內消法。施點陰膠法。內次服仙方活命飲。外以鐵箍散。見

後而亦愈用雲物四調物湯。方內點陰膠法。用次服

膠云即是陰膠所用在口。中起雲氣直達至陰膠處。住雷處知少痛足可醫也。即知陰

公府之欲隱所而痛。在在黑垢達至太乙膏持。少許口中即服。附以生薑服。

膠而吐膿滑內吐微起者。肺癰也。黑肺直面而乾。陰膠太乙膏持乙香附以生薑服。

振中肺府之癰隱而痛患者。滿肺陰膠上。內吐微起者師也。其人入。緊飲燥。

振起寒發熱。數尺膿在。腹中吐嗽為肺。血膿其其。吐脈入。緊飲燥。

translation:
Method of Applying Yin Adhesive (Point Yin Gum Treatment)

Lung Abscess (Fei Yong)

Internal Symptoms: For consumption-type conditions, use the Internal Dispersing Method. Apply the Point Yin Adhesive Method, then take the Immortal Formula Life-Saving Decoction (Xianfang Huoming Yin) internally, and externally apply Iron Binding Powder (Tiehu San). See below for further details. One may also recover using the Four-Substance Regulating Decoction with Cloud Substance. Apply the Point Yin Adhesive Method, then take the next prescribed dose.

The Yin Adhesive works by sending its medicinal vapor — rising like clouds — directly to the site of the Yin Adhesive in the body, reaching the place of pain associated with thunder. If there is slight pain at the feet, this indicates the physician has located the correct point. One should know immediately where the Yin adhesive has reached.

When the patient feels hidden pain in the area of the lung府 (organ system), and there is phlegm in the mouth — if upon applying the Yin Adhesive the patient expels thin, foamy sputum, this indicates lung abscess. Apply Taiyi Gao (Supreme Unity Plaster) with a small amount held in the mouth and swallowed, supplemented with fresh ginger.

When the lung abscess is hidden and painful, and the patient's lungs are full — if thin, foamy sputum is produced, the condition belongs to this category of disease. The patient's breathing is labored and thirst is pronounced.

When the patient has chills followed by fever, and pus is found in the abdomen, and there is coughing — this is lung abscess. The pulse is tight and there is dry thirst.

After eating, if cold sensation remains and the condition has not yet fully formed into a tight, consolidated abscess — this still constitutes an abscess condition. When large amounts of pus form in the abdomen, it becomes a true lung abscess. The face is pale and the patient expectorates pus.

If the pulse indicates the condition has not yet consolidated — it can overcome the metal element. If the pulse is floating, the abscess has already formed and is difficult to treat. The face is pale and the patient expectorates pus.

When there is shortness of breath, fullness in the stomach, and heat with coughing of blood — the condition becomes like paste and is very difficult to treat. The physician must proceed carefully with such a cough.

For patients with red complexion, shortness of breath, and gastric fullness — when pus forms and then stops, and the condition becomes paste-like — treatment is difficult. The physician must manage the cough carefully.

For those with fetid discharge, first palpate and examine. In lung abscess cases where wind-type deficiency causes lassitude and internal fullness with coughing — if the condition resembles the aunt's intestinal yin pain pattern — one must first release the exterior with multiple doses. Use Suzi (Perilla) Decoction for cough with internal phlegm. If the lung buds can still be saved before pus has fully consolidated, first administer Minor Blue-Green Dragon Decoction (Xiao Qinglong Tang).

Liver Abscess: Fever emanating from the Qimen acupoint with desire to vomit, fullness and pain in the chest and flanks — this is called liver abscess. When there is swelling and pain in the upper flesh, it is called liver abscess. When the pain is higher, it is called carbuncle. When the upper flesh slightly rises, it is liver abscess at an extreme stage.

When there is intense heat, acrid drying agents such as bupleurum are inappropriate. For those with rapid progression, add Chaihu-tang (Bupleurum Decoction). When swelling is mild in the intestinal area, arising from internal heat, the mass becomes hard.

When there is fever with dryness in the stool, bupleurum and medicines to clear liver heat are used. If fullness increases, reduce the amount and use medicines as appropriate. When internal heat causes hardness, do not proceed without reviewing.

Kidney Abscess: When the kidney area swells extending down to the lower abdomen, it is called kidney carbuncle. When the flesh above the kidney slightly rises, it is kidney abscess.

Dongui (Eastern Medicine)

Sixteen-Ingredient Qi-Flowing Drink (十六味流氣飲)

Stomach Abscess (胃脘癰)

[Ingredients include:] Gardenia fruit, kidney-supporting herbs, apricot kernel, coptis, forsythia — sixteen ingredients in total. This formula circulates qi and addresses skin redness. It promotes circulation, calms, disperses, and enters the skin layer to address dark [conditions].

[Ingredients:] Zhi Ke (bitter orange), Chai Hu (bupleurum), Wu Yao (lindera root), Sang Mu (mulberry wood), Chuan Xiong (ligusticum), Gui Zhi (cinnamon twig), Bai Shao (white peony), Ren Shen (ginseng), Dang Gui (angelica), Mian Huang (astragalus), Hou Po (magnolia bark), Zi Su Ye (perilla leaf), Da Fu Pi (areca husk), Gan Cao (licorice), Fang Feng (saposhnikovia), Mu Xiang (aucklandia root), Xue Men (blood gate herb). Six fen of each, made into one packet, decocted in water and taken. Add ginger.

The Yellow Emperor asked: When a patient has a stomach abscess, how is it diagnosed? Bo [Qi Bo] replied: Examine this — when the stomach pulse is fine and thin, qi gathers in the stomach region forming an abscess. The stomach pulse circulates throughout, and when qi accumulates, this indicates heat accumulation — the person has a stomach abscess.

When [qi] rushes inward to the stomach region but does not flow strongly, the stomach becomes ulcerated. If the stomach pulse is sunken and fine, this indicates cold turbid qi accumulating and filling [the area], leading to heat accumulation and stomach abscess.

When the bowel pulse is tight and tense, even though an abscess has not yet fully formed, there is already qi stagnation. When an abscess is present, the stomach pulse is surging and rapid; when it is sunken, there is qi stagnation forming an abscess.

The stomach region [is affected] because food stagnates and clear qi overflows, damaging the lung and causing the stomach region to wither. Directions for treatment are found in the external symptoms section: coughing, vomiting, alternating chills and fever.

When phlegm and pain cause stomach tightness and fullness, the lung loses its nourishment and true pulse is disturbed, causing the stomach to wither. Treatment directions are found in the external symptoms section. For coughing, use Gan [Cao formula].

[Use] Dihuang (rehmannia) decoction, Ganjiang (dried ginger) powder — these may be taken as appropriate. Also see the Yuncee (cloud tablet) chapter for reducing and dispersing formulas, or for cough [treatment].

Dongyuan Tuoli San (Li Dongyuan's Expelling Pus Powder):
Ingredients: Water decoction taken continuously. Yinhua, Xiaohua, Danggui 6 fen; Chixiong, Shaoyao, Dahuang, Huangqi each 4 fen; Zaojiao thorn 1 piece. Apply as a plaster with wine. Treats stomach abscess, swellings, carbuncles, and internal suppurations; for boils beginning to form pus, malignant sores at initial onset — disperses and eliminates them, or brings them to drainage; also for wounds from metal implements.
